A map of every tool installed by this repo, organised by the manager that
owns it. Companion to [`upgrades.md`](upgrades.md) — that one is the

===== pitfalls/brew-bundle-redownloads-manually-installed-cask.md =====
# `brew bundle` re-downloads & fails on cask whose `.app` is already in `/Applications/`

**Symptoms** (grep this section):

- `brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin` prints `Fetching <cask>` for an app the user has already installed (e.g. by dragging the `.app` into `/Applications/` from a vendor DMG)
- Logs include `A `brew fetch warp cursor ... discord ... ` process has already locked
  /Users/<u>/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads/<sha>--<File>.dmg.incomplete. Please wait for it to finish or terminate it to continue.` for many casks at once
- ``brew bundle` failed! Failed to fetch warp, cursor, visual-studio-code, claude, chatgpt, ...` at the end of the run
- Same Brewfile applies cleanly on the **source** mac where the user `brew install --cask`'d things, but breaks on a **second** mac where many `.app`s were dragged in manually before `chezmoi apply` was first run
- `brew list --cask <name>` exits non-zero even though `/Applications/<Name>.app` exists
- `chezmoi apply` succeeds at the chezmoi level but `[WARN] Some packages in macOS packages from Brewfile.darwin still failed after 2 attempts (continuing...)` appears in the log

**First seen**: 2026-05 on `Hanrus-Mac-mini` (mac-mini with many `.app`s pre-dragged into `/Applications/`, then `chezmoi update --init` from a different machine's `Brewfile.darwin`)
**Affects**: any macOS host where casks declared in `~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin` have `.app` artifacts already present in `/Applications/` but no corresponding entry in `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/<name>/.metadata/`
**Status**: **partially mitigated** in `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl`. The stale-lockfile half (`clear_brew_download_locks` + retry pass) is permanently on. The `--adopt` pre-flight half is **opt-in** via `CHEZMOI_BREW_ADOPT_PREFLIGHT=1` — see "Why `--adopt` is opt-in" below. Upstream `--adopt` was added in [Homebrew/brew#14033](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/pull/14033) closing [#14006](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/issues/14006).

## Symptom

```console
$ chezmoi apply
...
[INFO] Installing macOS packages from Brewfile.darwin...
Fetching warp, cursor, visual-studio-code, claude, chatgpt, antigravity, codex-app, codeisland, ollama-app, ...
Fetching: warp, cursor, visual-studio-code, claude, ...
✘ Cask warp (0.2026.05.06.15.42.stable_04)
Error: A `brew fetch warp cursor visual-studio-code claude chatgpt ...` process has already locked /Users/<u>/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads/d7b851c68d6ffb0fc9008aa6d18ccb31feff009339ae656932de009c7057b1a3--Warp.dmg.incomplete.
Please wait for it to finish or terminate it to continue.
✘ Cask cursor (3.3.30,...)
Error: A `brew fetch ...` process has already locked /Users/<u>/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads/7bf557fd...--Cursor-darwin-arm64.zip.incomplete.
Please wait for it to finish or terminate it to continue.
... (many more)
`brew bundle` failed! Failed to fetch warp, cursor, visual-studio-code, claude, chatgpt, ...
[INFO] Retrying macOS packages from Brewfile.darwin (attempt 2/2, only missing items)...
... (retry hits identical .incomplete locks)
[WARN] Some packages in macOS packages from Brewfile.darwin still failed after 2 attempts (continuing...)
```

```console
$ ls /Applications/Discord.app                 # the app IS already there
/Applications/Discord.app
$ brew list --cask discord                     # but brew doesn't know about it
Error: Cask 'discord' is not installed.
$ ls /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/discord/.metadata/ # no metadata directory
ls: /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/discord/.metadata/: No such file or directory
```

## Root cause

Two cascading issues:

1. **Drag-installed `.app` is invisible to Homebrew.** `brew bundle` checks `Caskroom/<name>/.metadata/<version>/` to decide "already installed." A `.app` you copied manually into `/Applications/` has no Caskroom entry, so brew thinks it's missing and queues it for download. There's no auto-detection of pre-existing `.app`s in `/Applications/` — by design, because brew can't safely assume the version matches what its cask definition expects.
2. **Parallel-fetch lockfile contention.** When `brew bundle` schedules a re-download of many large casks at once, `brew fetch` runs them in parallel and each download claims `~/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads/<sha>--<file>.incomplete` plus a sibling lockfile. If any prior `brew fetch` was interrupted (Ctrl-C, terminated, previous failed `chezmoi apply`), the stale `.incomplete*` files cause every fresh attempt to error out instantly with `process has already locked …`. The bundle's own retry loop then hits the same stale locks on attempt 2 and gives up.

The two failure modes are independent but co-occur: (1) makes brew try to re-download apps you already have, and (2) makes that re-download cascade into many parallel locked-file errors at once.

## Why `--adopt` is opt-in (the field-tested findings)

The first implementation of the adopt pre-flight ran unconditionally. Real-world testing on `Hanrus-Mac-mini` (22 casks in `Brewfile.darwin`, ~half drag-installed) revealed four reasons `--adopt` isn't the clean win the upstream PR description suggests:

1. **`--adopt` does NOT fast-fail on a missing artifact.** brew's cask installer always runs `fetch_artifacts` (download) BEFORE `install_artifacts` (where the `--adopt` branch decides adopt-or-error). So `brew install --cask --adopt cursor` when `/Applications/Cursor.app` doesn't exist will still download `Cursor-darwin-arm64.zip` (~150MB from cursor.com CDN, painfully slow on CN networks) and only THEN raise `Error: It seems there is no installed App at '/Applications/Cursor.app' to adopt`. Our script now filesystem-prefilters by `/Applications/*.app` presence to avoid this — but that only catches the "missing" case, not the "present-but-mismatched" case below.

2. **`--adopt` is byte-exact strict.** brew compares the downloaded artifact's SHA256 against `/Applications/<App>.app`. If your manually-installed version is anything other than the *exact* current brew-formula version, brew raises an error and falls back to a full install (downloads, then overwrites). In one real-world apply, only **8 of 19** filtered casks actually adopted; the other 11 hit version mismatch (user had v3.3.30 of Cursor, brew expected v3.3.32, etc.) and re-downloaded anyway. Net win on first apply: ~36%.

3. **Password storm.** Each `brew install --cask --adopt` invocation internally shells out to `sudo /usr/sbin/installer` (pkg-based casks) or `sudo xattr` (quarantine bit removal) or similar. Our `sudo_session_warm_cache` warms the TTY timestamp once, but brew's internal sudo invocations don't always reuse it — they may `sudo -k` first or use a different timestamp_type. Observed: one `Password:` prompt per pkg-based cask, with multi-second gaps where the user must babysit the terminal.

4. **Mac App Store conflicts.** Casks whose vendor also ships via the App Store (e.g. `tailscale-app`) pop up an interactive *"Mac App Store Install Detected"* dialog mid-apply when brew runs the cask's pkg installer. The opt-in version detects this via `mas list` and skips those casks, but you'd never know to look for it otherwise.

Combined, the unconditional pre-flight cost the user ~15 minutes of password-babysitting and re-downloads to save ~3 minutes of bundle-install work. Hence: opt-in.

## When opting in IS worthwhile

`export CHEZMOI_BREW_ADOPT_PREFLIGHT=1` in `~/.shellrc.adhoc` if:

- You're setting up a new mac.
- You have just `chezmoi init`'d from a source machine and are about to first-apply.
- Most apps you've manually dragged into `/Applications/` happen to be the current brew-formula versions (rare in practice — vendor auto-updaters drift the .app forward faster than Brewfile gets refreshed).
- You can tolerate sitting at the terminal to feed `Password:` prompts.

Otherwise, leave it off. `brew bundle`'s normal download path is slower one-time but doesn't require babysitting, and once a cask is brew-tracked subsequent applies are fast.

## Workaround (manual, no script)

If you want to run adopt manually without enabling the env var:

```bash
# 1. Clear stale lockfiles from any interrupted prior fetch
rm -f ~/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads/*.incomplete*

# 2. Try adopting (slow + interactive — expect password prompts)
HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew bundle list --casks --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin | while IFS= read -r cask; do
    short="${cask##*/}"
    [[ -d /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/$short ]] && continue   # already tracked
    # Pre-filter: only try if /Applications/ has a likely match
    /bin/ls -1 /Applications | grep -iqE "^${short//-/[ -]?}.*\.app$" || continue
    brew install --cask --adopt "$cask" 2>&1 | head -2
done

# 3. Re-run brew bundle
HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin --no-upgrade
```

## Prevention

- `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl` exports `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` + `HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_UPGRADE=1` to avoid the implicit `brew update` that can transiently fail on Aliyun mirror sync lag (`Unable to find <sha> under https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew/brew.git`). Upgrades go through `just upgrade-*`, per `CLAUDE.md → "Install vs upgrade is split on purpose"`.
- The bundle retry loop calls `clear_brew_download_locks` between attempts to wipe any `*.incomplete*` files left over from a previous interrupted fetch. This is permanently on (not opt-in) — it's pure win, no downsides.
- The `adopt_existing_casks` pre-flight runs only when `CHEZMOI_BREW_ADOPT_PREFLIGHT=1` is set (see "Why opt-in" above). When enabled it also: (a) filesystem-pre-filters casks by `/Applications/*.app` presence so non-existent .apps don't trigger a download, (b) checks `mas list` to skip App Store conflicts, (c) captures brew's first stderr line on failure so you can see *why* an adopt failed.
- When adding a new cask to `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`, don't pre-emptively delete any existing `/Applications/<Name>.app` — even if adopt won't help (version mismatch), the cask will install correctly on first apply.

===== pitfalls/tailscale-another-copy-app-store-leftover.md =====
# "Another Tailscale copy was found on this Mac" + DNS unavailable

**Symptoms** (grep this section):
- Tailscale debug → System Configuration Inspector: `System Configuration Issue Found` / `A software conflict and/or installation error on your Mac has been detected` / `Another Tailscale copy was found on this Mac.` / `Another copy of Tailscale was found at this path: /Applications/Tailscale.localized/Tailscale.app` / `onlyOneCopyExplainer`
- `Current Issues` → `DNS Unavailable` / `Tailscale can't reach the configured DNS servers` / `Code: dns-forward-failing`
- `mdfind -name "Tailscale.app"` returns **two** paths: `/Applications/Tailscale.app` **and** `/Applications/Tailscale.localized/Tailscale.app`
- macsys menu-bar app keeps flagging the conflict even after quitting/reopening
- (related, second trap) `brew upgrade --cask tailscale-app` prints `Removing files: /usr/local/bin/tailscale` and re-creates it; a later `brew upgrade tailscale` / `brew link tailscale` warns `Target /usr/local/bin/tailscale already exists` — the **formula and cask fight over `/usr/local/bin/tailscale`**

**First seen**: 2026-07
**Affects**: macOS. (1) The `.localized` leftover bites any host that installed Tailscale from the Mac App Store **before** this repo migrated `mas "Tailscale"` → `cask "tailscale-app"` (May 2026). (2) The formula/cask CLI-path conflict bites any host that had **both** `cask "tailscale-app"` and the standalone `brew "tailscale"` formula installed.
**Status**: fixed — delete the leftover; use the **cask only** (no `tailscale` formula on macOS)

## Symptom

Two independent Tailscale `.app` bundles coexist. The **running** one is the
macsys standalone build (installed by `cask "tailscale-app"`); the **idle** one
is the old sandboxed App Store build, sitting in a `.localized` wrapper folder:

```
$ mdfind -name "Tailscale.app"
/Applications/Tailscale.localized/Tailscale.app
/Applications/Tailscale.app

$ for p in /Applications/Tailscale.app /Applications/Tailscale.localized/Tailscale.app; do
    echo "$p → $(defaults read "$p/Contents/Info.plist" CFBundleIdentifier)  $(defaults read "$p/Contents/Info.plist" CFBundleShortVersionString)"
  done
/Applications/Tailscale.app                       → io.tailscale.ipn.macsys  1.98.8   # cask, RUNNING, system extension
/Applications/Tailscale.localized/Tailscale.app   → io.tailscale.ipn.macos   1.98.8   # App Store leftover, idle
```

The `dns-forward-failing` / DNS Unavailable banner tends to ride along with the
conflict (two IPN clients confusing the network-extension / DNS proxy state).

## Root cause

Two collisions, both stemming from **install-only** package management:

### 1. App Store `.app` leftover (the "Another copy" warning)

Two Tailscale variants exist for macOS, with *different bundle IDs and signing
chains* — macOS treats them as separate apps:

- `io.tailscale.ipn.**macsys**` — standalone build, Developer ID-signed
  (`Developer ID Application: Tailscale Inc. (W5364U7YZB)`), runs a **system
  extension** as the daemon. This is what `cask "tailscale-app"` installs.
- `io.tailscale.ipn.**macos**` — sandboxed **Mac App Store** build, re-signed by
  Apple (`Apple Mac OS Application Signing`). Installed into a
  `/Applications/Tailscale.localized/` wrapper folder.

This repo migrated `mas` → `cask` in May 2026 (Tailscale was delisted from the
Mac App Store — `mas` install now fails with `No apps found in the App Store for
ADAM ID 1475387142`; see `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`). `chezmoi
apply` is **install-only** and does not uninstall the previously `mas`-installed
copy, so it lingers. The macsys installer takes `/Applications/Tailscale.app`
and shoves the old copy aside into `.localized/`, producing the warning.

(`_MASReceipt` exists in **both** bundles, so it is *not* a reliable
discriminator — use `CFBundleIdentifier` `macsys` vs `macos`, or the `codesign
-dv --verbose=4` Authority line, to tell them apart.)

### 2. `tailscale` formula vs `tailscale-app` cask fight over the CLI path

The `tailscale-app` **cask/pkg already installs the CLI** at
`/usr/local/bin/tailscale` — a tiny root-owned shell wrapper into the app:

```
$ cat /usr/local/bin/tailscale
#!/bin/sh
/Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/tailscale "$@"
```

So the separate standalone **`brew "tailscale"` formula is redundant** on a
GUI-app host. Worse, both the formula (via its `/usr/local/bin/tailscale`
symlink into the Cellar) and the cask (via the pkg wrapper) target the **same
path** — whoever installs/upgrades last wins, so `brew upgrade tailscale` and
`brew upgrade --cask tailscale-app` clobber each other. The formula also ships a
`/usr/local/bin/tailscaled` the app's system extension already provides — a
daemon that must **never** run on macOS. Same shape as
[`ollama-brew-link-fails-cask-shadows-formula`](ollama-brew-link-fails-cask-shadows-formula.md).

## Workaround

**Delete the idle App Store leftover** (root-owned → needs `sudo`). The running
macsys cask app and your tailnet login are untouched:

```bash
sudo rm -rf /Applications/Tailscale.localized
```

The "Another Tailscale copy" warning clears once the second `.app` is gone.
Optionally purge the stale sandbox container:

```bash
rm -rf ~/Library/Containers/io.tailscale.ipn.macos ~/Library/Group\ Containers/*.io.tailscale.ipn.macos 2>/dev/null || true
```

**Drop the redundant formula** so nothing fights the cask over the CLI path. The
cask's `/usr/local/bin/tailscale` wrapper is a pkg file, not brew-managed, so
`brew uninstall` leaves it in place — the CLI keeps working:

```bash
brew uninstall tailscale                 # removes the formula + its stray tailscaled symlink
tailscale version                        # still 1.98.8 via the cask wrapper
```

Keep the cask current (`auto_updates`, but a running server may need a nudge):

```bash
HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew upgrade --cask tailscale-app   # sudo + may re-approve the system extension
```

## Prevention

- **Cask only on macOS. No `tailscale` formula.** The repo's shared
  `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.tmpl` carries an explicit "deliberately no
  `brew \"tailscale\"`" note in the darwin block — do not re-add it. The GUI app
  (`cask "tailscale-app"`, Brewfile.darwin) *is* the daemon **and** the CLI.
- **NEVER `brew services start tailscale` on macOS.** Homebrew's own post-install
  caveat suggests it, but the app's system extension is the daemon; a second
  `tailscaled` conflicts.
- **Prefer Standalone (cask) over App Store** — see `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`
  ("Standalone > App Store"). Do **not** re-add a `mas "Tailscale"` entry (it's
  delisted anyway).
- Fresh installs don't hit either trap (no App Store copy, no formula). These
  only bite hosts that predate the `mas → cask` migration or that once had the
  formula installed alongside the cask.

## Related

- `docs/tools/Tailscale.md` — install preference (Standalone > App Store) + this cleanup
- `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl` — `cask "tailscale-app"` + delisted-`mas` note
- `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.tmpl` — darwin block's "deliberately no formula" note
- `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` — A–Z row for `tailscale-app`
- [`ollama-brew-link-fails-cask-shadows-formula`](ollama-brew-link-fails-cask-shadows-formula.md) — same formula-vs-cask path fight
- [`macfuse-too-old-unsupported-macos-version-rclone-mount`](macfuse-too-old-unsupported-macos-version-rclone-mount.md) — another `auto_updates` cask that `brew upgrade` won't move

# `chezmoi apply` dies at llm_tools: `brew link` step did not complete (ollama)

<!-- Symptom = the brew link failure; root cause = the ollama-app cask symlink
     shadows the CLI-only formula. Grep terms: "brew link", "Could not symlink
     bin/ollama", "ollama", "shadowed by /usr/local/bin/ollama". -->

**Symptoms** (grep this section):

- `chezmoi apply` / `chezmoi apply --init` aborts in the `llm_tools` ansible role:
  ```
  [87] TASK · [llm_tools : Install Ollama via Homebrew formula (macOS CLI install)]
  [ERROR]: Task failed: Module failed: ✔︎ Bottle ollama (0.30.10)
  Error: The `brew link` step did not complete successfully
  Origin: /Users/david/.ansible/roles/llm_tools/tasks/main.yml:90:3
  ...
  ✘ fatal: [localhost]: FAILED! (23.9s) =>
      changed: false
      msg: |-
          ✔︎ Bottle ollama (0.30.10)
          Error: The `brew link` step did not complete successfully
  ...
  chezmoi: .chezmoiscripts/global/20_ansible_roles.sh: exit status 2
  ```
- Running the link by hand spells out the conflict:
  ```
  $ brew link ollama
  Error: Could not symlink bin/ollama
  Target /usr/local/bin/ollama
  already exists. You may want to remove it:
    rm '/usr/local/bin/ollama'

  To force the link and overwrite all conflicting files:
    brew link --overwrite ollama
  ```
- `brew info ollama` shows the bottle is installed but **not linked**, with a
  shadow caveat:
  ```
  ==> Caveats
  The following ollama executables are shadowed by other commands earlier in your PATH:
    ollama (shadowed by /usr/local/bin/ollama)
  ```
- The colliding target is a symlink into the **GUI app**, not a stray file:
  ```
  $ readlink /usr/local/bin/ollama
  /Applications/Ollama.app/Contents/Resources/ollama
  $ brew list --cask | grep -i ollama
  ollama-app
  ```
- Because the play aborts mid-run, every role tagged **after** `llm_tools`
  (`networking_tools`, `tunnel_tools`, `iac_tools`, `media_tools`,
  `dotnet_tools`) silently never runs — `PLAY RECAP` shows `failed=1` and the
  remaining roles are simply absent.

**First seen**: 2026-06 on `Hanrus-MacBook-Pro` (Intel, macOS 26.3.1) during
`chezmoi apply --init` with `installBrewApps=false`. The host had picked up the
`ollama-app` cask months earlier (a prior apply with `installBrewApps=true`),
then a later apply with `installBrewApps=false` tried to add the CLI-only
formula on top.
**Affects**: macOS hosts where the **`ollama-app` cask** (GUI runtime) is
installed AND the `llm_tools` role's formula path runs (i.e.
`installBrewApps=false`). Both Intel (`/usr/local/bin/ollama`) and Apple
Silicon (`/opt/homebrew/bin/ollama`). Any tool with both a cask that drops a
CLI shim and a same-named formula can hit the identical trap.
**Status**: fixed in `dot_ansible/roles/llm_tools/tasks/main.yml` — a
`which ollama` pre-check now gates the formula install so it never fights an
existing CLI.

## Root cause

Two Homebrew packages want the **same** link target `…/bin/ollama`:

| Package | Kind | Provides | When this repo installs it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ollama-app` | cask (GUI) | `Ollama.app` + a `…/bin/ollama` symlink into the app bundle | `Brewfile.darwin` when `installAiDesktopApps && installLlmTools` |
| `ollama` | formula (CLI) | `…/Cellar/ollama/<v>/bin/ollama`, linked into `…/bin/ollama` | `llm_tools` role when `installBrewApps=false` |

`brew install ollama` pours the bottle fine, then auto-runs `brew link`, which
**refuses to clobber** the cask's existing symlink and exits non-zero. The
ansible `community.general.homebrew` module surfaces that as a task failure and
the whole play aborts.

The role's original guard was the wrong signal:

```yaml
when:
  - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  - not (llm_tools_install_brew_apps | bool)   # ← proxy, not the real conflict
```

`llm_tools_install_brew_apps` (← the `installBrewApps` prompt) is only a *proxy*
for "did we install GUI apps this run". It does **not** detect a cask that a
*previous* run (or a manual `brew install --cask ollama-app`) already dropped on
disk. The real question is simply: **is there already an `ollama` on PATH?** If
yes, the formula is redundant and linking it can only collide.

> Note the gating is doubly mismatched: the cask is gated on
> `installAiDesktopApps && installLlmTools`, while the formula-skip was gated on
> `installBrewApps`. So the proxy can't even be made consistent — only the
> on-disk "is there an ollama CLI" check is reliable.

## Workaround

**The durable fix (already in the role):** pre-check for an existing CLI and
skip the formula when one is present.

```yaml
- name: Check whether an ollama CLI is already present (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  ansible.builtin.command: which ollama
  register: llm_tools_ollama_macos_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Install Ollama via Homebrew formula (macOS CLI install)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
    - not (llm_tools_install_brew_apps | bool)
    - llm_tools_ollama_macos_check.rc != 0   # ← only if no ollama CLI yet
  community.general.homebrew:
    name: ollama
    state: present
```

**To clean up a host that's already in the half-installed state**, pick the
end-state you want — the app and the formula both provide a working `ollama`
CLI, so you only need one:

```sh
# A) Keep the GUI app (it already provides the CLI) — drop the redundant formula
brew uninstall ollama
which ollama   # -> /usr/local/bin/ollama -> /Applications/Ollama.app/...

# B) Go CLI-only — remove the app, then link the formula (now unobstructed)
brew uninstall --cask ollama-app
brew link ollama
```

Do **not** reach for `brew link --overwrite ollama` as the fix: it makes the
formula win *this* time, but you still have two installs fighting over the same
path, and an app self-update will recreate its symlink and re-break linking.

**To finish the aborted apply** (the post-`llm_tools` roles never ran), just
re-run `chezmoi apply`. If chezmoi thinks the ansible run-script is unchanged
and skips it, force the one script to re-run:

```sh
chezmoi state delete --bucket=entryState \
  --key="$HOME/.chezmoiscripts/global/20_ansible_roles.sh"
chezmoi apply
```

## Prevention

- Guard package installs on the **observable end-state** (`which <tool>`), not a
  prompt/role-var proxy, whenever a sibling package can already provide the same
  binary. The proxy var answers "did the user opt into X this run", which is a
  different question from "is X already on disk".
- When a tool ships **both** a cask-with-CLI-shim and a same-named formula,
  assume some hosts will end up with both. Installing the second one must be a
  no-op, not a hard error.
- Remember that an ansible task failure **aborts the whole play** — a single
  brew-link collision silently drops every later role. After any mid-run
  failure, assume the tail of the role list didn't run and re-apply.

## Related

- Sibling brew/cask trap: [`brew-bundle-redownloads-manually-installed-cask.md`](brew-bundle-redownloads-manually-installed-cask.md)
  — same family (cask vs already-present `.app`), different mechanism (bundle
  re-download vs formula link collision).
- Sibling Homebrew-on-apply trap: [`homebrew-6-refuses-untrusted-tap-formula.md`](homebrew-6-refuses-untrusted-tap-formula.md)
  — another "`chezmoi apply` dies in an ansible homebrew task" failure mode.
- Source of the fix: `dot_ansible/roles/llm_tools/tasks/main.yml` (the
  `Check whether an ollama CLI is already present (macOS)` pre-check).
- GUI side of the gating: `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`
  (`cask "ollama-app"` under `installAiDesktopApps && installLlmTools`).
- Latent follow-up (not yet fixed): the cask-gate (`installAiDesktopApps &&
  installLlmTools`) and the formula-gate (`installBrewApps`) can disagree, so
  `installBrewApps=true` + `installAiDesktopApps=false` installs *no* ollama at
  all. The `which ollama` guard doesn't cover that case (the `not
  install_brew_apps` condition short-circuits first).
```

## 結論先講

**沒有單一的通用指令**能告訴你「這個 app 是怎麽裝的」,但**每個平台都有可靠的訊號**,把它們**按「專屬程度」排成一棵決策樹**就能判斷。核心原則(這 repo 的 `ollama` pitfall 剛好印證):**判斷「磁碟上現在是誰擁有這個檔案」,而不是靠某個代理變數**——從最專屬的 package manager 往下 fall through,沒人認領才算「手動安裝」。

而且要小心:**有些看似權威的訊號其實不可靠**(下面 macOS 的 `_MASReceipt` 就是活生生的坑)。

---

## macOS —— 給一個 `.app` bundle

按這個順序問,先命中的就是答案:

| 順序 | 來源 | 判斷指令 | 註記 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Homebrew cask** | `ls "$(brew --prefix)/Caskroom/<name>/.metadata"` 存在 → brew 追蹤中;或 `brew list --cask` | ⚠️ 手動拖進 `/Applications` 的 `.app` **沒有** Caskroom entry,即使有對應 cask,`brew list --cask` 也會說沒裝(見 `brew-bundle-redownloads-manually-installed-cask` pitfall) |
| 2 | **Mac App Store** | `mas list`;或 `mdls -name kMDItemAppStoreHasReceipt Foo.app` → `1` | ⚠️ **`Contents/_MASReceipt/receipt` 不可靠**——Tailscale 的坑裡,App Store 版和 standalone 版**兩個 bundle 都有** `_MASReceipt`。要用下面第 4 列的簽章來區分 |
| 3 | **Direct download (pkg 安裝器)** | `pkgutil --pkgs` + `pkgutil --file-info /path` | pkg 才有 receipt;拖 dmg 進去的不會有 |
| 4 | **Direct download (dmg / 瀏覽器下載)** | `xattr -p com.apple.metadata:kMDItemWhereFroms Foo.app`(或 `mdls -name kMDItemWhereFroms`)→ 真正的下載 URL;`xattr -p com.apple.quarantine` → 哪個 agent 下載的 | 這是最直接的「出處」證據 |

**最能一刀切的判別是簽章**(`codesign -dv --verbose=4 /Applications/Foo.app` 看 `Authority=`):

- `Apple Mac OS Application Signing` → **App Store**(Apple 會把所有上架 app 重簽)
- `Developer ID Application: <Vendor> (TeamID)` → **cask 或直接下載**(這兩者簽章相同,得靠上表第 1/4 列再分)

還有一招辨識「同一個 app 被裝了兩份」:`mdfind -name "Foo.app"` 列出所有副本,再 `defaults read Foo.app/Contents/Info.plist CFBundleIdentifier` 看 bundle ID(Tailscale 就是 `io.tailscale.ipn.macsys` cask 版 vs `io.tailscale.ipn.macos` App Store 版)。

---

## Ubuntu / Linux —— 給一個指令或 app

先 `realpath "$(command -v foo)"` 解出真實路徑(GUI app 則看 `.desktop` 的 `Exec=`),再按順序:

| 順序 | 來源 | 判斷 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **snap** | 路徑在 `/snap/` 下(`/snap/bin/foo` 是 symlink 到 `/usr/bin/snap`);`snap list` |
| 2 | **flatpak** | `flatpak list`;檔案在 `/var/lib/flatpak` 或 `~/.local/share/flatpak`;靠 `flatpak run` 啓動 |
| 3 | **apt / dpkg** | `dpkg -S <realpath>` 印出擁有它的套件 → **這是最權威的檢查**(RPM 系:`rpm -qf`)。再用 `apt-mark showmanual` 分辨是你手動裝還是被當相依拉進來的 |
| 4 | **Linuxbrew** | 路徑在 `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew` 或 `~/.linuxbrew`;`brew list` |
| 5 | **AppImage** | 單一可執行檔、`dpkg -S` 查不到、`file foo` 顯示內嵌 squashfs;通常在 `~/Applications` / `~/.local/bin` |
| 6 | **語言型 pm**(cli) | pip/pipx/cargo/npm/mise/uv/go/gem → 路徑落在 `~/.cargo/bin`、mise shims、`~/.local/share/uv` 等 |
| 7 | **手動 `make install`** | `/usr/local/` 且 `dpkg -S` 查不到 → 沒人認領 |

⚠️ 一個常見誤會:**「Ubuntu Software / App Store」不是一種後端**,它只是 GNOME Software / Snap Store 這個 *前端*,底下裝下來的其實就是 **deb(apt)或 snap**。所以「怎麽從 App Store 裝的」= 判斷是 deb 還是 snap 即可。

# In-house CLI skeleton — exact conventions

There are **two distinct archetypes** in this repo. Pick based on complexity:

- **Umbrella launcher + package** (`yth`, `mlf`, `fleet`): thin Python dispatcher at `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_<name>` + a `scripts/<name>/` package (`__init__.py` shared helpers + one leaf module per subcommand, each using **tyro**).
- **Single-file** (`pqsum`, `sms`, `mi-router`, `reyee`): everything in `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_<name>`, **argparse** (pqsum) or tyro (mi-router). **`scripts/pqsum/` does not exist** — pqsum is fully self-contained in its 44k launcher.

---

## 1. Launcher boot pattern (self-boots via `uv run --script` + PEP723)

Every launcher is a PEP723 inline-script run directly by `uv` — **not** a bash wrapper, and **not** `uv run --with`. The shebang uses `env -S`. Verbatim headers:

`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_yth` (lines 1-10):
```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "yt-dlp>=2025.1",
#   "tyro>=0.9",
#   "rich>=13.9",
#   "platformdirs>=4",
# ]
# ///
```

`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mlf` (lines 1-11): identical shebang; deps `mlflow>=3.4`, `tyro>=0.9`, `rich>=13.9`, `plotext>=5.2`, `textual>=5.0`.

`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_pqsum` (lines 1-7): identical shebang; deps just `rich>=13.9` (it shells out to agent CLIs rather than importing an SDK).

**Locating `scripts/<name>/`** — umbrella launchers trust `chezmoi source-path`, fall back to `~/.local/share/chezmoi`, then `sys.path.insert`. Verbatim from `executable_yth` (identical in `executable_mlf`, called `_source_path`, "Identical strategy to executable_fleet"):
```python
def _source_path() -> Path:
    chezmoi = shutil.which("chezmoi")
    if chezmoi:
        try:
            out = subprocess.run(
                [chezmoi, "source-path"],
                capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, timeout=5,
            )
            if out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout.strip():
                return Path(out.stdout.strip())
        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError):
            pass
    fallback = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "chezmoi"
    if (fallback / "scripts" / "yth" / "__init__.py").is_file():
        return fallback
    print("yth: cannot locate chezmoi source dir. ...", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)
```
Then in `main()`:
```python
src = _source_path()
if str(src) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(src))
```

**Dispatch pattern** (umbrella): `main()` handles `-h/--help/help` *before* any heavy import (keeps `yth -h | grep` fast, never loads yt_dlp), then routes `sys.argv[1]` to leaf modules. Two styles coexist:
- `mlf` uses a `dispatch = {name: fn}` dict of `_dispatch_*` closures (lines 203-216).
- `yth` uses a `leaves = {sub: (module, prog)}` table + a `_leaf()` that rewrites `sys.argv` and imports the leaf module:
```python
def _leaf(module: str, prog: str, args: list[str]) -> int:
    sys.argv = [prog, *args]
    mod = __import__(f"scripts.yth.{module}", fromlist=["main"])
    return mod.main()
```
Bare invocation (no args) execs the Television picker (`os.execvp(tv, [tv, "yth", *args])`) for yth, or the Textual TUI for mlf. Short action shims (`open`/`copy`/`play`) call helpers in `scripts/<name>/__init__.py` directly.

---

## 2. Python module layout

`scripts/yth/` (package): `__init__.py` (17k, shared helpers), `enrich.py`, `fetch_subs.py`, `import_takeout.py`, `list.py`, `search.py`, `show.py`, `sync.py` — one file per subcommand, hyphen→underscore (`fetch-subs`→`fetch_subs.py`).

`scripts/mlf/` (package): `__init__.py` (shared), `tui.py` (61k Textual), `plot.py`, `list.py`, `download.py`.

`scripts/pqsum/`: **does not exist** — single-file.

**`__init__.py` = the shared-helper home** (CLAUDE.md rule: "Shared helpers live in `scripts/<name>/__init__.py` — refactor there, not in call sites"). `scripts/yth/__init__.py` holds: `APP = "yth"`, path helpers (`data_dir`/`config_dir`/`cache_dir`/`db_path`), the sqlite `_SCHEMA` + `connect()`, id/URL parsing, config/cookie loading, a **lazy** heavy-dep importer (`def ytdl(): import yt_dlp; return yt_dlp`), and the `open_id`/`copy_id`/`play_id` action helpers the launcher shims import. `scripts/mlf/__init__.py` mirrors this: lazy `make_client()`, `open_id`/`copy_id` (identical pbcopy→wl-copy→xclip→OSC52 chain), `detect_kind`, `fetch_histories`. Both docstrings note heavy deps are imported lazily so hot/DB-only paths and `-h` stay instant.

---

## 3. Arg parsing

**Umbrella leaf modules → tyro.** Each leaf declares a `@dataclass Args` with `Annotated[...tyro.conf.arg(...)]` fields and a uniform `main()`. Verbatim from `scripts/yth/search.py`:
```python
import tyro

@dataclass
class Args:
    query: Annotated[
        list[str], tyro.conf.Positional,
        tyro.conf.arg(help="Search terms (ANDed). Quote to include spaces."),
    ] = field(default_factory=list)
    subs: Annotated[bool, tyro.conf.arg(help="Also search indexed caption text.")] = False
    json_out: Annotated[bool, tyro.conf.arg(name="json", help="Emit JSON instead of a table.")] = False
    limit: Annotated[int, tyro.conf.arg(help="Max results.")] = 50
    raw: Annotated[bool, tyro.conf.arg(help="Pass the query straight to FTS5 ...")] = False

def main() -> int:
    return cli(tyro.cli(Args, prog="yth search"))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```
Note the **`--json` convention**: the field is named `json_out` (since `json` is a stdlib name) but exposed to the user as `--json` via `tyro.conf.arg(name="json", ...)`. `tyro.cli(Args, prog="...")` is always passed the `prog` so help text is correct after the launcher rewrites `sys.argv`.

**Single-file pqsum → argparse**, with a positional `mode` subcommand. Verbatim `parse_args()` (lines 1025-1041):
```python
def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="pqsum", description="pueue queue summary ...")
    p.add_argument("mode", nargs="?", default="text", choices=["text", "ai", "json"])
    p.add_argument("-g", "--group", default="", help="Restrict to one pueue group.")
    p.add_argument("--stdin-json", action="store_true", ...)
    p.add_argument("-r", "--refresh", action="store_true", help="Bypass cache.")
    p.add_argument("--no-cache", action="store_true", ...)
    ...
    return p.parse_args()
```
Here JSON is a whole `mode` (`pqsum json`) rather than a `--json` flag.

**JSON emission**, two idioms:
- yth leaves: plain `json.dumps(results, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)` over lists of dicts (`search.py:137`).
- pqsum: dataclasses → `asdict` → `json.dumps(..., default=str)`:
  ```python
  if args.mode == "json":
      print(json.dumps([asdict(s) for s in snapshots], indent=2, default=str))
  ```

## 4. Dataclass / JSON schema pattern (pqsum)

`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_pqsum` lines 138-182, `from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field`:
```python
@dataclass
class TaskRec:
    id: int
    status: str
    result: str | None            # "Success" / "Failed" / "Killed" / etc.
    exit_code: int | None
    group: str
    command: str
    label: str | None
    created_at: str | None
    start: str | None
    end: str | None
    duration_s: float | None

@dataclass
class GroupRec:
    name: str
    daemon_status: str
    parallel_tasks: int
    total: int
    done: int
    pct: float
    total_spent_s: float | None
    avg_done_s: float | None
    eta_s: float | None
    status_breakdown: dict[str, int]
    failed_task_ids: list[int]

@dataclass
class HostSnapshot:
    host: str
    daemon_reachable: bool
    error: str | None
    total_tasks: int
    total_done: int
    overall_pct: float
    avg_done_s: float | None
    eta_s: float | None
    status_breakdown: dict[str, int]
    groups: list[GroupRec] = field(default_factory=list)
    tasks: list[TaskRec] = field(default_factory=list)
```
Serialized with `json.dumps([asdict(s) for s in snapshots], indent=2, default=str)`. **Cross-tool contract** (CLAUDE.md line 20): these keys are consumed by `scripts/fleet/pueue.py` (`pqsum json --raw-stdin` → `pqsum ai --stdin-json`), so adding/renaming a field silently breaks fleet's AI mode — update both in one commit. (yth uses a sqlite schema instead of dataclasses; the equivalent contract there is the `_SCHEMA` string in `scripts/yth/__init__.py:120`.)

## 5. Caching — dominant convention

**Two families exist; pick by data kind:**

**(A) Transient/derived cache → `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` with `~/.cache` fallback, subdir = tool name.** This is the convention for a *cache* specifically. pqsum's full implementation (`executable_pqsum` lines 610-652) is the reference skeleton:
```python
_CACHE_VERSION = "v1"

def _cache_path(prompt_hash: str) -> Path:
    base = os.environ.get("XDG_CACHE_HOME") or os.path.expanduser("~/.cache")
    d = Path(base) / "pqsum"
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    host = socket.gethostname().split(".")[0] or "host"
    return d / f"{host}-{prompt_hash}.json"

def _cache_lookup(prompt_hash: str) -> tuple[dict | None, str]:
    p = _cache_path(prompt_hash)
    if not p.is_file():
        return None, "miss"
    try:
        data = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
        return None, "miss"
    if data.get("version") != _CACHE_VERSION:      # schema-version invalidation
        return None, "miss"
    if data.get("prompt_hash") != prompt_hash:     # key match
        return None, "miss"
    age = time.time() - float(data.get("generated_at", 0))
    parsed = data.get("parsed")
    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
        return None, "miss"
    if age > PQSUM_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL > 0:       # TTL (default 120s)
        return parsed, "stale-hit"
    return parsed, "hit"

def _cache_save(prompt_hash: str, parsed: dict) -> None:
    p = _cache_path(prompt_hash)
    p.write_text(json.dumps({
        "version": _CACHE_VERSION,
        "prompt_hash": prompt_hash,
        "generated_at": time.time(),
        "parsed": parsed,
    }, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
```
**Cache key/invalidation**: key = `sha256(prompt).hexdigest()[:16]` computed in `main()` (line 1068); the on-disk record is invalidated by (a) `version` mismatch, (b) `prompt_hash` mismatch, (c) age > TTL `PQSUM_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL` (env, default 120s). Filename embeds short hostname: `<host>-<hash>.json`. User overrides: `-r/--refresh` bypasses read; `--no-cache` skips read+write.

Same `XDG_CACHE_HOME or ~/.cache` idiom in `scripts/fleet/exec.py:472` and `executable_agent-warmup:85`. `scripts/fleet/apply.py` uses a fixed subdir `~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/{logs,sudo.pass}`.

**(B) Durable data/config (and platform-correct paths) → `platformdirs`.** yth (`scripts/yth/__init__.py:38-62`) and sms (`executable_sms`) use `user_data_dir(APP)` / `user_config_dir(APP)` / `user_cache_dir(APP)`; `platformdirs>=4` is in their PEP723 deps. yth puts its sqlite DB in `user_data_dir`, config in `user_config_dir`, and only scratch in `user_cache_dir`.

**Recommendation for a new CLI's cache:** if you just need a derived/regenerable JSON cache, copy pqsum's `$XDG_CACHE_HOME → ~/.cache/<tool>/` block verbatim (version + key + TTL). If the tool also has durable data/config and must be correct on macOS *and* Linux, use `platformdirs` like yth and let `user_cache_dir(APP)` give you the cache dir (on Linux that resolves to the same `~/.cache/<tool>` anyway).

---

## 6. PEP723 + ansible dual-declaration

`dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml` — deps that back an in-house CLI are declared in **both** the launcher's PEP723 block (so the tool self-bootstraps on first run, before ansible) **and** here (to `uv tool install` the package and expose its *standalone* binary on PATH). Verbatim entries:
```yaml
  - name: mlflow
    binary: mlflow
    needs_modern_gcc: true  # sqlalchemy -> greenlet C++ ext needs proper C++11 ...
  ...
  # yt-dlp: powers the in-house `yth` CLI ... Also declared in executable_yth's
  # PEP723 block so `yth` self-bootstraps even before ansible runs; this entry
  # additionally exposes the standalone `yt-dlp` binary on PATH (same dual
  # pattern as `mlflow` ↔ `mlf`). Pure Python, single entry point.
  - name: yt-dlp
    binary: yt-dlp
```
So: `mlflow` (dep of `mlf`) and `yt-dlp` (dep of `yth`) each appear twice. Each ansible entry is `{name, binary}` plus optional `with:` (extra deps), `with_executables_from:`+`extra_binaries:` (expose extra entry points), `python:` (pin), `needs_modern_gcc:` (skip on CentOS7-era gcc when it pulls numpy 2.x/pandas). `tyro`/`rich`/`platformdirs`/`plotext`/`textual` are *not* in the ansible list — they're pure library deps with no standalone binary, so PEP723-only is sufficient. **Rule of thumb:** add an ansible entry only if the dependency also ships a useful standalone binary; otherwise the PEP723 block alone bootstraps it.

---

## Files to copy for a new umbrella CLI `foo`

- `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_foo` — copy `executable_yth` (191 lines) or `executable_mlf` (221 lines); replace name, PEP723 deps, `USAGE`, dispatch table.
- `scripts/foo/__init__.py` — copy `scripts/yth/__init__.py` skeleton: `APP="foo"`, path helpers, lazy heavy-dep importer, `open_id`/`copy_id` helpers.
- `scripts/foo/<subcommand>.py` — copy `scripts/yth/list.py` (121 lines) or `search.py` — the minimal `@dataclass Args` + tyro + `main()` shape.
- Cache: paste pqsum's `_cache_path/_cache_lookup/_cache_save` (lines 610-652) into `__init__.py`.
- `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml` — add an entry only for deps that ship a standalone binary.
- Not covered here but flagged by CLAUDE.md lines 27-28 as required companions for a new CLI: shell completions (`dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_foo_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/<NN>_foo_completion.bash`, Strategy B hand-written like fleet/mlf/pqsum/x), an optional `tv` channel (`dot_config/television/cable/foo.toml`), a docs page (`docs/tools/foo.md`), and possibly a mention in the agent-facing `dot_agents/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles/SKILL.md.tmpl`.

### Representative subcommand pattern — `fleet` (COPY THIS for `scan`/`which`)

Because your CLI has subcommands (not pqsum's single positional mode), `fleet` is the correct template. The full files are at `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/zsh/tools/45_fleet_completion.zsh` and `.../dot_config/bash/45_fleet_completion.bash`.

**zsh — guard + dispatcher + per-subcommand + dynamic helper** (verbatim excerpts):

```zsh
# 45_fleet_completion.zsh - tab completion for `fleet` (fleet-apply umbrella).
(( $+commands[fleet] )) || return 0

# Dynamic helper: shells out to the CLI itself
_fleet_hosts_one() {
    local -a hosts
    hosts=( ${(f)"$(fleet hosts --list 2>/dev/null)"} )
    (( ${#hosts} )) && _describe -t hosts 'fleet host' hosts
}

# Per-subcommand flags via _arguments
_fleet_tmux() {
    _arguments \
        '--hosts=[comma-separated host names]:hosts:_fleet_hosts_csv' \
        '--json[emit JSON]' \
        '--deep[include visible pane area (slower)]'
}

# Top-level dispatcher
_fleet() {
    local context state state_descr line
    typeset -A opt_args
    _arguments -C \
        '1: :->subcommand' \
        '*::arg:->args'
    case "$state" in
        subcommand)
            local -a subs=(
                'chezmoi:Chezmoi-specific deploy ops (apply/status/diff/tail/kill/compact)'
                'tmux:Cross-host tmux session summary'
                'info:Cross-host system status snapshot'
            )
            _describe -t subcommands 'fleet subcommand' subs
            ;;
        args)
            case "$line[1]" in
                chezmoi) _fleet_chezmoi ;;
                tmux)    _fleet_tmux ;;
                info)    _fleet_info ;;
            esac
            ;;
    esac
}
compdef _fleet fleet
```

Your `scan`/`which` with `--json` maps directly: subcommand list `(scan which)`, and each `_appsrc_scan` / `_appsrc_which` declares `'--json[emit JSON]'` plus any flags. For a dynamic `which <APP>` candidate that shells out, copy `_fleet_hosts_one` (it runs `fleet hosts --list`; yours would run e.g. `appsrc scan --list` or `appsrc which --list`).

# Mirrors dot_config/zsh/tools/45_fleet_completion.zsh — keep both in sync.

_fleet_hosts_one() {                       # dynamic helper (shells out)
    local cur="$1"; local hosts
    hosts=$(fleet hosts --list 2>/dev/null)
    COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$hosts" -- "$cur") )
}

_fleet_completion() {                      # top-level dispatcher
    local cur prev words cword
    _init_completion -n = || return
    if [ "$cword" -eq 1 ]; then
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "chezmoi edit tmux info pueue exec hosts" -- "$cur") )

            esac
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "--hosts --json --deep" -- "$cur") )

    esac
}
complete -F _fleet_completion fleet

## Surface 2 — Television (tv) channel — OPTIONAL

**No registration step.** Channels are auto-discovered by globbing `~/.config/television/cable/*.toml`; `channels.toml` itself is just a browse-channel over that glob, and `docs/tools/tv.md:610-613` confirms *"Channels are defined as `.toml` files in `~/.config/television/cable/`"*. So adding a channel = drop one new file:

- Create: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/apps.toml` (or `apps.toml.tmpl` if the source command is OS-specific — mac-apps/linux-apps/mac-procs use `.tmpl` gated on `{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" }}`).

**Closest analogue for "browse all installed apps + their install source":** a hybrid of `fleet-hosts.toml` (thin channel that shells out to the CLI for source/preview/action — best if `appsrc` emits its own rows) and `mac-apps.toml.tmpl` (per-row lifecycle actions with Alt-gated keybindings).

**Verbatim skeleton (thin, shells-out-to-CLI style — from `fleet-hosts.toml`):**

```toml
[metadata]
name = "fleet-hosts"
description = "Fleet hosts (from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)"
requirements = ["fleet", "ssh"]

[source]
command = "fleet hosts --list-tsv"
# Lines look like:   name<TAB>target<TAB>kind
display = "{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"

[preview]
command = "fleet hosts --describe '{split:\\t:0}'"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:connect"
alt-t = "actions:probe"
alt-s = "actions:status"

[actions.connect]
description = "SSH into the selected fleet host"
command = "fleet hosts '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "execute"
```

For an apps-browser, your `[source]` would be `appsrc scan --json` or a TSV (`name<TAB>version<TAB>source`), `display`/`output` split on `\t`, `[preview]` = `appsrc which '{split:\\t:0}'`, and keybindings for actions (open, copy install command, reveal in Finder). Note the structural pieces present in every channel: `[metadata]` (name/description/`requirements = [...]` for gating), `[source]` (`command`, `display`, `output`, optional `no_sort`), `[preview]` (`command`, optional `header`), optional `[ui]`/`[ui.preview_panel]`, `[keybindings]` (`enter`, `alt-*`, `ctrl-*`), and one `[actions.<name>]` block per action with `description` + `command` + `mode` (`execute` for interactive/paged, `fork` for fire-and-forget).

**Keybinding convention (load-bearing, from `mac-apps.toml.tmpl:35-36` and CLAUDE.md row 33):** use **`Alt+`** not `Ctrl+` for custom actions — tmux's root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows inner apps; `ctrl-b` never reaches tv (tmux prefix). `mlflow.toml` overrides tv's default `ctrl-y` with an id-only copy — do the same if you want copy-id.

If you add a channel with cross-platform mac/linux variants, CLAUDE.md **row 33** requires both `tv` channel files share Alt-key bindings where the verb exists on both sides.

## Surface 6 — justfile — OPTIONAL convention

File: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/justfile`. There **is** a per-CLI umbrella-recipe convention: a `<name> *ARGS:` passthrough that runs the source-tree binary via `uv run --script` (so it works before the first `chezmoi apply`). Verbatim (lines 514–525):

```make
# Umbrella `fleet` CLI — same binary chezmoi deploys to ~/.dotfiles/bin/fleet,
# but run from the source tree (works before first `chezmoi apply`). Subcommands:
# apply / status / diff / tail / kill / compact / edit / tmux / info / pueue.
# Prefer this over `fleet-*` recipes when invoking from inside the repo;
# the old recipes stay as muscle-memory aliases.
fleet *ARGS:
    @uv run --script ./dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet {{ARGS}}

# MLflow CLI umbrella — wraps `tv mlflow` plus open / copy / plot / list /
# download subcommands. See dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mlf for surface.
mlf *ARGS:
    @uv run --script ./dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mlf {{ARGS}}
```

Your recipe (add near these, only if the CLI is a `uv run --script` Python tool with an inline PEP 723 deps block, like fleet/mlf):
```make
appsrc *ARGS:
    @uv run --script ./dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_appsrc {{ARGS}}
```
If `appsrc` is a plain bash script (no uv deps), a just recipe adds little value and can be skipped — it's genuinely optional; not every in-house CLI has one (`pqsum`, `x`, `yth`, `wake` have no dedicated recipe).

# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos_intel`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`, or read `docs/tools/<name>.md`. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`view-office`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) in the terminal; also powers the yazi Office previewer. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~40 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`, `kill-process`, `services`,
`sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`, `mac-apps`/`linux-apps`. Full
reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` (or `prefix + e`) opens the action menu;
  `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools. Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,

## 1. The `app-*` helper layer

### macOS — `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl`
Gated by `{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}`. Public verbs:
`appquit`, `applaunch`, `appactivate`, `apprestart` (lifecycle) and `apprunning`, `applist`, `appresponsive` (inspection). Backend is entirely **osascript / Apple Events** — no filesystem enumeration of `/Applications` at all.

Key point for you: **`applist` does NOT enumerate installed apps** — it lists *running foreground processes* via System Events, not the `/Applications` directory:
- default: `name of every application process whose background only is false`
- `--pids`: `(unix id of p) & tab & (name of p)` per process
- `--all`: `name of every process`

So there is **no `/Applications` glob you can reuse** on the macOS side. You'll build the directory enumeration yourself.

### Linux — `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl`
Gated by `{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "linux" -}}`. Same 7 public verbs (cross-platform muscle memory, enforced by CLAUDE.md — see §5), plus a registry verb `linux_app_register`. Backend: `gtk-launch` / `gio launch` + `pkill -TERM -f` + optional GNOME `window-calls` D-Bus.

**This file is your biggest reuse win for Linux enumeration.** Two private helpers already iterate the canonical `.desktop` directory set:

`_linuxapp_lookup_desktop()` (lines 170-199) and the `applist` auto-derive loop (lines 456-484) both scan exactly:
```sh
for _d in /usr/share/applications "$HOME/.local/share/applications" \
          /var/lib/flatpak/exports/share/applications \
          "$HOME/.local/share/flatpak/exports/share/applications" \
          /var/lib/snapd/desktop/applications; do
```
and parse each `.desktop` with `awk -F=` for `Name=`, `StartupWMClass=`, `Exec=`, stripping `%f`/`%u` field codes via `sed -E 's/[[:space:]]+%[a-zA-Z]+//g'`. This is the proven idiom to copy for "enumerate GUI apps on Linux." Note the load-bearing subtlety already learned here (line 470): auto-discovery **requires an absolute `Exec=` path** to rule out `flatpak run …`/snap wrapper lines.

`applist` also writes running state; it is *not* a plain installed-apps enumerator (it only emits apps with a live pgrep match, except `--all`). So you can reuse the *scan loop* but not `applist` itself as your inventory source.

### tv channels — how they source the app list
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/mac-apps.toml.tmpl` (`{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}`): `[source].command` **inlines** the same osascript running-process query (lines 49) rather than calling `applist`, explicitly "so this channel works even before chezmoi-apply deploys the helper file." Actions re-source the helper: `. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && appquit '{split:\t:1}'`.
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/linux-apps.toml.tmpl` (`{{- if and (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") (eq .profile "ubuntu_desktop") -}}`): `[source].command` = `sh -c '. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh 2>/dev/null && applist --pids'`.

Both source running processes, output `<pid>\t<name>`, split on tab for display/output. **Neither is a manager-detection source** — confirming a detector is a new concern.

Line 734 has an important framing note: "Ubuntu Software / App Store" is **not a backend** — it's a GNOME Software/Snap Store *frontend* over deb-or-snap.

Reuse the *snapshot-once* technique (`ls -1 … | tr` into a variable, match in-memory) to avoid per-app forks.
- **Linux directory set:** **Fully covered already** — copy the 5-directory `.desktop` scan loop from `56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` (lines 174-177 / 456-459): `/usr/share/applications`, `~/.local/share/applications`, `/var/lib/flatpak/exports/share/applications`, `~/.local/share/flatpak/exports/share/applications`, `/var/lib/snapd/desktop/applications`. The `awk -F=` field extraction and the "absolute-Exec-path only" filter are already debugged there.

## 4. Caching precedent for slow scans

Multiple mature cache idioms exist; the **dominant, best-fit-for-you** one is **pqsum's**.

**`/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_pqsum:608-652`** — the canonical XDG JSON cache:
- Path: `Path(os.environ.get("XDG_CACHE_HOME") or "~/.cache") / "pqsum" / f"{host}-{prompt_hash}.json"` (per-host, keyed by a content hash).
- Envelope fields: `version` (`_CACHE_VERSION = "v1"`), `generated_at` (epoch `time.time()`), plus payload. On read: reject on JSON error, `version` mismatch, or key mismatch → `"miss"`; compute `age = time.time() - generated_at`; if `age > PQSUM_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL(=120s)` → `"stale-hit"` else `"hit"`. CLI flags `--refresh` (bypass read) and `--no-cache`.
- This is a **timestamp/age-in-JSON** staleness model (not raw file mtime). For a per-app scan cache, mirror it: `~/.cache/<yourtool>/<host>-<scan>.json` with `version` + `generated_at` + a per-app map; optionally key each entry on the app bundle's own mtime so a reinstalled app invalidates just its row.

Other precedents (for reference / alternative shapes):
- **fleet-apply** (`/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/fleet/apply.py`): actual on-disk layout is `~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/logs/<run_id>.log` + `.exit` sentinel (lines 321-330, 516-542, 695-711); GC keeps N newest by `p.stat().st_mtime` (line 705); liveness via `os.kill(pid, 0)`. **Note:** CLAUDE.md:177 describes an idealized `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}` that does **not** match the code — the code uses `chezmoi-fleet/logs/`. Don't copy the CLAUDE.md path literally.
- **chezmoi reload sentinel** (`/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh:26`): `_CZ_RELOAD_SENTINEL="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/chezmoi/last-apply"` — pure **mtime sentinel** (touch-file, compare mtimes), the lightest idiom.
- **tv lan-scan** (`docs/tools/tv.md:76-112`): `~/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv` + per-host `~/.cache/tv/lan-ports/<ip>.txt`, incremental **atomic `mv` of tmp over target**, `flock` on `~/.cache/tv/lan-scan.lock` for single-writer — the pattern to copy if your scan streams rows into a `tv` channel.
- **tsum** (`~/.cache/tmux-session-summary/<host>-<mode>.json` with a `version` field for auto-invalidation) — same shape as pqsum.

**Dominant idiom to adopt:** `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/<tool>/<host>-<key>.json`, JSON envelope with `version` + `generated_at` (epoch), age-based staleness threshold, `--refresh`/`--no-cache` flags, atomic tmp+`mv` write, optional `flock` if concurrent.

---

## 5. Cross-file update rule (CLAUDE.md) — should the detector stay out of it?

The rule is `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/CLAUDE.md:33`. Summary:

> The `app-*` helpers form a **4-file mirrored contract**: `dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl` ↔ `dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` ↔ `dot_config/television/cable/mac-apps.toml.tmpl` ↔ `dot_config/television/cable/linux-apps.toml.tmpl`. Both **shell helpers MUST expose the SAME public verb names** (`appquit`/`applaunch`/`appactivate`/`apprestart`/`apprunning`/`applist`/`appresponsive`). Adding a new verb to one side requires deciding whether it can be implemented on the other; if not, document the gap in `backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md`. Both `tv` channels **MUST share Alt-key bindings** where a verb exists on both sides (Alt+H is mac-only by design). Per-app Linux runtime-path overrides live in `~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf` (never auto-generated).

**Recommendation: keep the detector standalone — do NOT add an `appsource` verb into the 4-file contract.** Reasons, all supported by the evidence above:
1. The contract is a **symmetric lifecycle-verb** guarantee. A provenance detector is inherently **asymmetric** (macOS uses codesign/mas/Caskroom; Linux uses dpkg/snap/flatpak) — adding it as a mirrored verb would immediately force a "document the gap" exception and pollute a clean contract.
2. Your stated requirements — **batch scan when run with no args**, `--json`, caching, and `which`-style single-app query — match the **standalone `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*` CLI** shape (uv PEP-723 launcher: `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script` with an inline `# /// script` deps block, as in `executable_pqsum`/`executable_mlf`/`executable_yth`), not a sourced shell function.
3. Today's design transcript reached the same conclusion and the user explicitly chose the "full CLI" option (`:754-756`).

The correct cross-file obligations for a **new standalone CLI** (separate from the app-* contract) are the generic in-house-CLI ones: add zsh + bash completions (`dot_config/zsh/tools/45_*` / `dot_config/bash/45_*` pattern, cf. fleet completion files) and add a reverse-link in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` (exists, 90k) — which the transcript at `:740` notes is currently an *author-intent* index, not a runtime detector, so your tool complements it rather than duplicating it.

**Net reuse map:** copy the Linux `.desktop` scan loop + `awk` parsing from `56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl`; copy the arch-aware Caskroom resolver + `/Applications` snapshot + `mas list` snapshot from `run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl`; copy the `pkgutil` receipt idiom from `run_once_before_02_fix_intel_homebrew.sh.tmpl`; copy the pqsum JSON cache envelope; lift both detection decision tables verbatim from the today transcript + cookbook; heed the Tailscale `_MASReceipt`-is-unreliable pitfall. 90	    if not secs:

98	def iso_utc(value: str | None) -> str | None:
99	    """Normalize a timestamp string to ISO8601 UTC, or None if unparseable.
100	
101	    Takeout ``time`` fields look like ``2024-01-02T03:04:05.678Z``. We accept
102	    the trailing ``Z`` (Python <3.11 datetime.fromisoformat can't) and drop
103	    sub-second precision so ``watch_events`` de-dupes cleanly.
104	    """
105	    if not value:

110	    except ValueError:
111	        return None

246	def extract_video_id(url: str | None) -> str | None:
247	    """Pull an 11-char YouTube id out of a watch/short/embed/youtu.be URL.
248	
249	    Returns None for non-video rows (Google search entries, removed-video
250	    placeholders, anything without a recognisable id) so callers can skip
251	    them. Also accepts a bare id.

253	    if not url:
254	        return None
255	    url = url.strip()
256	    if VIDEO_ID_RE.match(url):
257	        return url

259	    from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse
260	
261	    try:
262	        u = urlparse(url)
263	    except ValueError:
264	        return None
265	    host = (u.hostname or "").lower().removeprefix("www.")
266	
267	    if host == "youtu.be":
268	        cand = u.path.lstrip("/").split("/")[0]
269	        return cand if VIDEO_ID_RE.match(cand) else None
270	
271	    if host in ("youtube.com", "m.youtube.com", "music.youtube.com"):
272	        if u.path == "/watch":
273	            vals = parse_qs(u.query).get("v", [])
274	            cand = vals[0] if vals else ""
275	            return cand if VIDEO_ID_RE.match(cand) else None
276	        for prefix in ("/shorts/", "/embed/", "/live/", "/v/"):
277	            if u.path.startswith(prefix):
278	                cand = u.path[len(prefix):].split("/")[0]
279	                return cand if VIDEO_ID_RE.match(cand) else None
280	    return None

319	def _detect_zen_profile() -> str | None:
320	    """Best-effort path to a Zen (Firefox fork) profile dir with cookies.
321	
322	    macOS: ``~/Library/Application Support/zen/Profiles/*/cookies.sqlite``.
323	    Linux: ``~/.zen/*/cookies.sqlite``. Returns the profile dir (not the
324	    sqlite file) since that's what yt-dlp's ``firefox:<path>`` wants. None
325	    when Zen isn't installed (the common case on this host).
326	    """
327	    roots = [

329	        Path.home() / ".zen",
330	    ]
331	    for root in roots:
332	        if not root.is_dir():
333	            continue
334	        hits = sorted(root.glob("*/cookies.sqlite"))
335	        if hits:
336	            return str(hits[0].parent)
337	    return None

372	_VTT_TAG = re.compile(r"<[^>]+>")  # <00:00:01.234>, <c>…</c>, alignment tags

375	def vtt_to_text(vtt: str) -> str:
376	    """Flatten a WebVTT subtitle blob to deduplicated plain text.
377	
378	    Strips the WEBVTT header, cue-timing lines, cue numbers, NOTE/STYLE
379	    blocks and inline ``<…>`` tags, then collapses the rolling-caption
380	    duplication typical of YouTube auto-subs (each cue repeats the previous
381	    visible line) with a simple ``line != last`` guard.
382	    """
383	    out: list[str] = []
384	    last: str | None = None
385	    for raw in vtt.splitlines():
386	        line = raw.strip()
387	        if (
388	            not line
389	            or line == "WEBVTT"
390	            or "-->" in line
391	            or line.isdigit()
392	            or line.startswith(("Kind:", "Language:", "NOTE", "STYLE"))
393	        ):
394	            continue
395	        line = _VTT_TAG.sub("", line).strip()
396	        if line and line != last:
397	            out.append(line)
398	            last = line
399	    return " ".join(out)

405	def fts_query(text: str) -> str:
406	    """Build a safe FTS5 MATCH string: AND of double-quoted terms.
407	
408	    Raw user input can contain ``-``, ``:``, ``"``, ``*``, ``(`` which are
409	    FTS5 operators and raise ``fts5: syntax error``. Quoting each whitespace
410	    term (doubling embedded quotes) turns everything into literal phrase
411	    tokens. Empty input yields ``""`` which the caller must special-case.
412	    """
413	    terms = [t for t in text.split() if t]
414	    return " ".join('"' + t.replace('"', '""') + '"' for t in terms)

422	    ident = video_id.strip()
423	    if not VIDEO_ID_RE.match(ident):
424	        print(f"yth open: not a valid video id: {ident!r}", file=sys.stderr)
425	        return 2
426	    import webbrowser
427	
428	    url = video_url(ident)
429	    print(f"[yth] open: {url}", file=sys.stderr)
430	    if not webbrowser.open(url):
431	        print(
432	            "yth open: no usable browser opener (open/xdg-open/wslview missing).\n"
433	            f"  URL: {url}",
434	            file=sys.stderr,
435	        )
436	        return 1
437	    return 0
438	
439	
440	def copy_id(video_id: str) -> int:
441	    """Copy the video URL to the clipboard. Returns exit code.
442	
443	    Provider chain pbcopy → wl-copy → xclip → OSC 52, matching
444	    ``scripts/mlf.copy_id`` and the ``yth.toml [actions.copy-url]`` snippet.
445	    """
446	    ident = video_id.strip()
447	    payload = video_url(ident) if VIDEO_ID_RE.match(ident) else ident
448	    providers = [["pbcopy"], ["wl-copy"], ["xclip", "-selection", "clipboard"]]
449	    for cmd in providers:
450	        if shutil.which(cmd[0]):
451	            try:
452	                subprocess.run(cmd, input=payload, text=True, check=True)
453	            except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
454	                print(f"yth copy: {cmd[0]} failed ({e.returncode})", file=sys.stderr)
455	                continue
456	            print(f"[yth] copied via {cmd[0]}: {payload}", file=sys.stderr)
457	            return 0
458	    try:
459	        import base64
460	
461	        b64 = base64.b64encode(payload.encode()).decode()
462	        with open("/dev/tty", "w") as tty:
463	            tty.write(f"\033]52;c;{b64}\007")
464	        print(f"[yth] copied via OSC52: {payload}", file=sys.stderr)
465	        return 0
466	    except OSError as e:
467	        print(f"yth copy: no clipboard provider and OSC52 failed ({e}).", file=sys.stderr)
468	        return 1
469	
470	
471	def play_id(video_id: str, cfg: dict | None = None) -> int:
472	    """Play in mpv when configured + installed, else open in browser."""
473	    ident = video_id.strip()
474	    if not VIDEO_ID_RE.match(ident):
475	        print(f"yth play: not a valid video id: {ident!r}", file=sys.stderr)
476	        return 2
477	    cfg = cfg if cfg is not None else load_config()
478	    url = video_url(ident)
479	    if cfg.get("open_target") == "mpv" and shutil.which("mpv"):
480	        print(f"[yth] mpv: {url}", file=sys.stderr)
481	        return subprocess.run(["mpv", url]).returncode
482	    return open_id(ident)
483
