1	{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
2	# shellcheck shell=sh
3	# app-* helpers — graceful control of macOS GUI apps via osascript / Apple Events.
4	#
5	# Why not `killall`? `killall AppName` sends SIGTERM and most GUI apps don't
6	# register a handler, so containers / unsaved buffers / background sync just
7	# die. `osascript -e 'tell application "X" to quit'` sends the Quit Apple
8	# Event — the same thing ⌘Q does — so the app tears down cleanly. Matters
9	# for OrbStack / Docker Desktop / Slack / any app with state.
10	#
11	# Frozen-app detection (`appresponsive`) is best-effort: macOS exposes the
12	# "Not Responding" flag only via Activity Monitor's private SPI. The public
13	# proxy is "send a no-op Apple Event with a short timeout — if it throws,
14	# the app is hung." False positives happen on apps mid-launch.
15	#
16	# All helpers take an app NAME (e.g. `OrbStack`, `Google Chrome`), not a
17	# bundle ID. `$1` is passed via osascript's `argv` so spaces and quotes in
18	# app names are handled correctly without shell-escaping gymnastics.
19	#
20	# Linux counterpart: dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl. Same public
21	# verb names (appquit / applaunch / appactivate / apprestart / apprunning /
22	# applist / appresponsive) but a different backend — gtk-launch + pkill -TERM
23	# + optional GNOME window-calls extension. Cross-platform muscle memory by
24	# design; per-platform gaps documented in
25	# backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md (Alt+H "hide" is mac-only — Linux
26	# can't hide windows without compositor IPC).
27	
28	_macapp_is_darwin() { [ "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" = "Darwin" ]; }
29	
30	_macapp_guard_darwin() {
31	    if ! _macapp_is_darwin; then
32	        printf 'app-helper: macOS-only (current OS: %s)\n' \
33	            "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" >&2
34	        return 1
35	    fi
36	}
37	
38	_macapp_need_name() {
39	    if [ -z "$1" ]; then
40	        printf 'usage: %s <AppName>\n  e.g. %s OrbStack\n' "$2" "$2" >&2
41	        return 2
42	    fi
43	}
44	
45	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
46	# Public: lifecycle
47	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
48	
49	# appquit NAME — send Quit Apple Event (graceful, equivalent to ⌘Q).
50	appquit() {
51	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
52	        printf 'usage: appquit <AppName>\n  Send Quit Apple Event (graceful shutdown).\n  Example: appquit OrbStack\n'
53	        return 0 ;;
54	    esac
55	    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
56	    _macapp_need_name "$1" appquit || return 2
57	    osascript \
58	        -e 'on run argv' \
59	        -e 'tell application (item 1 of argv) to quit' \
60	        -e 'end run' \
61	        -- "$1"
62	}
63	
64	# applaunch NAME — start the app in the background (no focus steal).
65	applaunch() {
66	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
67	        printf 'usage: applaunch <AppName>\n  Launch in background (no focus steal). Use appactivate to bring to front.\n'
68	        return 0 ;;
69	    esac
70	    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
71	    _macapp_need_name "$1" applaunch || return 2
72	    osascript \
73	        -e 'on run argv' \
74	        -e 'tell application (item 1 of argv) to launch' \
75	        -e 'end run' \
76	        -- "$1"
77	}
78	
79	# appactivate NAME — start (if needed) and bring to front.
80	appactivate() {
81	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
82	        printf 'usage: appactivate <AppName>\n  Launch + bring to front. Use applaunch for headless start.\n'
83	        return 0 ;;
84	    esac
85	    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
86	    _macapp_need_name "$1" appactivate || return 2
87	    osascript \
88	        -e 'on run argv' \
89	        -e 'tell application (item 1 of argv) to activate' \
90	        -e 'end run' \
91	        -- "$1"
92	}
93	
94	# apprestart NAME — quit, wait for shutdown, relaunch in background.
95	apprestart() {
96	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
97	        printf 'usage: apprestart <AppName>\n  Graceful quit + background relaunch. Useful after config edits.\n'
98	        return 0 ;;
99	    esac
100	    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
101	    _macapp_need_name "$1" apprestart || return 2
102	    appquit "$1" || return $?
103	    # Poll until really gone — `quit` returns before the app process exits.
104	    _macapp_i=0
105	    while [ "$_macapp_i" -lt 30 ] && apprunning "$1"; do
106	        sleep 0.5
107	        _macapp_i=$((_macapp_i + 1))
108	    done
109	    unset _macapp_i
110	    applaunch "$1"
111	}
112	
113	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
114	# Public: inspection
115	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
116	
117	# apprunning NAME — exit 0 if app is running, 1 otherwise. Silent.
118	apprunning() {
119	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
120	        printf 'usage: apprunning <AppName>\n  Exit 0 if running, 1 otherwise. Silent — use $? or && / ||.\n'
121	        return 0 ;;
122	    esac
123	    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
124	    _macapp_need_name "$1" apprunning || return 2
125	    _macapp_out=$(osascript \
126	        -e 'on run argv' \
127	        -e 'tell application "System Events" to return (exists (processes where name is (item 1 of argv)))' \
128	        -e 'end run' \
129	        -- "$1" 2>/dev/null)
130	    [ "$_macapp_out" = "true" ]
131	}
132	
133	# applist [--pids] — list visible (foreground) GUI apps, one per line.
134	# Default: just names. `--pids` adds PID + bundle path.
135	applist() {
136	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
137	        printf 'usage: applist [--pids|--all]\n'
138	        printf '  Default     names of visible foreground GUI apps, one per line.\n'
139	        printf '  --pids      "<pid>\\t<name>" via lsappinfo (foreground only).\n'
140	        printf '  --all       include background-only / agent processes.\n'
141	        return 0 ;;
142	    esac
143	    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
144	
145	    case "${1:-}" in
146	        --pids)
147	            # AppleScript exposes `unix id` directly — cleaner than parsing
148	            # `lsappinfo list` (which is multi-line and includes background
149	            # daemons mixed with foreground apps).
150	            osascript \
151	                -e 'tell application "System Events"' \
152	                -e '  set out to ""' \
153	                -e '  repeat with p in (every application process whose background only is false)' \
154	                -e '    set out to out & (unix id of p) & tab & (name of p) & linefeed' \
155	                -e '  end repeat' \
156	                -e '  return out' \
157	                -e 'end tell'
158	            ;;
159	        --all)
160	            osascript \
161	                -e 'tell application "System Events" to set procNames to name of every process' \
162	                -e 'set AppleScript'\''s text item delimiters to linefeed' \
163	                -e 'return procNames as text'
164	            ;;
165	        ""|*)
166	            osascript \
167	                -e 'tell application "System Events" to set procNames to name of every application process whose background only is false' \
168	                -e 'set AppleScript'\''s text item delimiters to linefeed' \
169	                -e 'return procNames as text'
170	            ;;
171	    esac
172	}
173	
174	# appresponsive NAME [TIMEOUT_SEC] — exit 0 if app responds within timeout.
175	# Sends a no-op Get-name Apple Event with `with timeout`. If AppleScript
176	# throws (timeout or "isn't running"), exit 1.
177	#
178	# Best-effort: this is the public-API proxy for "Not Responding". An app
179	# mid-launch may falsely fail; raise TIMEOUT (default 2s) to reduce noise.
180	appresponsive() {
181	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
182	        printf 'usage: appresponsive <AppName> [TIMEOUT_SEC]\n'
183	        printf '  Exit 0 if app answers an Apple Event within TIMEOUT (default 2s).\n'
184	        printf '  Exit 1 if hung, not running, or scripting-disabled.\n'
185	        printf '  Example: appresponsive OrbStack 5 || echo hung\n'
186	        return 0 ;;
187	    esac
188	    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
189	    _macapp_need_name "$1" appresponsive || return 2
190	    _macapp_to=${2:-2}
191	    apprunning "$1" || return 1
192	    _macapp_out=$(osascript \
193	        -e 'on run argv' \
194	        -e 'set t to (item 2 of argv) as integer' \
195	        -e 'with timeout of t seconds' \
196	        -e '  try' \
197	        -e '    tell application (item 1 of argv) to get name' \
198	        -e '    return "yes"' \
199	        -e '  on error' \
200	        -e '    return "no"' \
201	        -e '  end try' \
202	        -e 'end timeout' \
203	        -e 'end run' \
204	        -- "$1" "$_macapp_to" 2>/dev/null)
205	    unset _macapp_to
206	    [ "$_macapp_out" = "yes" ]
207	}

3	# app-* helpers — graceful control of Linux GUI apps.
4	#
5	# Linux counterpart to dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl. SAME public
6	# verb names (appquit/applaunch/appactivate/apprestart/apprunning/applist/
7	# appresponsive) so users get cross-platform muscle memory. Backends diverge
8	# by necessity:
9	#
10	#   applaunch     gtk-launch <desktop-id>            works for any .desktop
11	#   apprunning    pgrep -f <pattern>                 override or auto-derived
12	#   appquit       pkill -TERM -f <pattern>           Electron/Firefox honour SIGTERM
13	#   apprestart    appquit + poll-gone + applaunch
14	#   appactivate   gdbus → GNOME window-calls ext     ⚠ ext not installed →
15	#                 OR falls through to applaunch         apps' own re-focus
16	#   applist       enumerate registered + .desktop    ⚠ "managed apps that
17	#                                                       are alive"
18	#   appresponsive playerctl MPRIS probe              ⚠ MPRIS apps only;
19	#                 OR degrades to apprunning             no Linux analog to
20	#                                                       macOS Apple Events
21	#
22	# Override file: ~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf is sourced if present.
23	# Define apps via `linux_app_register NAME --desktop=ID --pkill=REGEX
24	# --wm-class=CLASS [--mpris=NAME]`. Auto-derivation handles unregistered
25	# apps via .desktop scan + Exec basename, but fails for AppImage runtime
26	# paths (see pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md).
27	#
28	# Backlog: backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md
29	# Playbook: docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md → "Controlling installed apps"
30	
31	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
32	# Guards
33	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
34	
35	_linuxapp_is_linux() { [ "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" = "Linux" ]; }
36	
37	_linuxapp_guard_linux() {
38	    if ! _linuxapp_is_linux; then
39	        printf 'app-helper: Linux-only (current OS: %s)\n' \
40	            "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" >&2
41	        return 1
42	    fi
43	}
44	
45	_linuxapp_need_name() {
46	    if [ -z "$1" ]; then
47	        printf 'usage: %s <AppName>\n  e.g. %s Cursor\n' "$2" "$2" >&2
48	        return 2
49	    fi
50	}

52	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
53	# Override registry (zsh + bash associative arrays; POSIX sh: skip)
54	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

56	if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
57	    typeset -gA _linuxapp_pkill _linuxapp_desktop _linuxapp_wmclass _linuxapp_mpris _linuxapp_exec
58	elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then

74	# linux_app_register NAME --desktop=ID --pkill=REGEX --wm-class=CLASS [--mpris=NAME]
75	linux_app_register() {
76	    case "$1" in
77	        -h|--help)
78	            cat >&2 <<'HELP'
79	linux_app_register NAME [OPTIONS]    register an app for app-* helpers
80	linux_app_register --list            print currently registered apps
81	
82	  --desktop=ID       .desktop file stem (zen-browser, cursor, discord)
83	  --exec=PATH        explicit launch command for apps with NO .desktop file
84	                     (manually-placed Electron apps, hand-built binaries).
85	                     Used by applaunch in preference to --desktop when set;
86	                     supports `~` expansion. Skip --desktop for these.

88	  --wm-class=CLASS   WM_CLASS (matches StartupWMClass=); used by appactivate
89	                     when the GNOME window-calls extension is installed

91	                     by appresponsive for the MPRIS probe
92	
93	  Typical call site: ~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf (sourced at startup).
94	
95	  Example:
96	    linux_app_register Spotify \
97	      --desktop=spotify_spotify \

121	    shift
122	
123	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do

140	# matches the .shellrc.secrets convention).

169	# latest-mtime .desktop file matching NAME by stem / Name= / StartupWMClass=.
170	_linuxapp_lookup_desktop() {

238	    # Echo desktop-id stem for NAME; exit 1 if unresolved.
239	    if [ -n "${_linuxapp_desktop[$1]:-}" ]; then
240	        printf '%s\n' "${_linuxapp_desktop[$1]}"
241	        return 0
242	    fi
243	    _row=$(_linuxapp_lookup_desktop "$1") || true
244	    if [ -n "$_row" ]; then
245	        printf '%s\n' "$_row" | cut -f1
246	        [ -n "$_row" ] && { unset _row; return 0; }
247	    fi
248	    unset _row
249	    return 1
250	}
251	
252	_linuxapp_resolve_wmclass() {
253	    if [ -n "${_linuxapp_wmclass[$1]:-}" ]; then
254	        printf '%s\n' "${_linuxapp_wmclass[$1]}"
255	        return 0
256	    fi
257	    _row=$(_linuxapp_lookup_desktop "$1") || true
258	    if [ -n "$_row" ]; then
259	        printf '%s\n' "$_row" | cut -f3
260	    fi
261	    unset _row
262	}
263	
264	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
265	# Public: lifecycle
266	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
267	
268	# applaunch NAME — launch via --exec= override, gtk-launch, or gio in background.
269	applaunch() {
270	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
271	        printf 'usage: applaunch <AppName>\n  Launch order:\n    1. --exec=PATH override (for apps without a .desktop file)\n    2. gtk-launch <desktop-id> resolved from override or .desktop scan\n    3. gio launch <full-desktop-path> as fallback\n  Example: applaunch Cursor\n'
272	        return 0 ;;
273	    esac
274	    _linuxapp_guard_linux || return 1
275	    _linuxapp_need_name "$1" applaunch || return 2
276	
277	    # 1. --exec= override wins — for manually-placed binaries with no .desktop.
278	    _ex=${_linuxapp_exec[$1]:-}
279	    if [ -n "$_ex" ]; then
280	        # eval to expand ~ and $HOME; treat the value as a shell-quoted command.
281	        _ex_expanded=$(eval "printf '%s' \"$_ex\"")
282	        (setsid -f sh -c "$_ex_expanded" >/dev/null 2>&1 &) 2>/dev/null \
283	            || nohup sh -c "$_ex_expanded" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
284	        unset _ex _ex_expanded
285	        return 0
286	    fi
287	    unset _ex
288	
289	    # 2. + 3. gtk-launch / gio launch via .desktop resolution.
290	    _id=$(_linuxapp_resolve_desktop "$1") || {
291	        printf 'applaunch: no .desktop file resolved for %s\n  Hint: linux_app_register %s --desktop=<id> ... OR --exec=<command>\n' "$1" "$1" >&2
292	        unset _id; return 3
293	    }
294	    if command -v gtk-launch >/dev/null 2>&1; then
295	        (setsid -f gtk-launch "$_id" >/dev/null 2>&1 &) 2>/dev/null \
296	            || nohup gtk-launch "$_id" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
297	    elif command -v gio >/dev/null 2>&1; then
298	        _f=$(_linuxapp_find_desktop_file "$_id") || {
299	            printf 'applaunch: .desktop file path not found for id=%s\n' "$_id" >&2
300	            unset _id _f; return 3
301	        }
302	        (setsid -f gio launch "$_f" >/dev/null 2>&1 &) 2>/dev/null \
303	            || nohup gio launch "$_f" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
304	        unset _f
305	    else
306	        printf 'applaunch: neither gtk-launch nor gio is installed\n' >&2
307	        unset _id; return 4
308	    fi
309	    unset _id
310	}
311	
312	# appquit NAME — SIGTERM the runtime process (graceful for Electron/Firefox).
313	appquit() {
314	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
315	        printf 'usage: appquit <AppName>\n  Send SIGTERM to the matching process (Electron + Firefox quit gracefully).\n  Pattern: override (~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf) or auto-derived from .desktop.\n'
316	        return 0 ;;
317	    esac
318	    _linuxapp_guard_linux || return 1
319	    _linuxapp_need_name "$1" appquit || return 2
320	    _pat=$(_linuxapp_resolve_pattern "$1") || {
321	        printf 'appquit: could not resolve runtime pattern for %s\n  Hint: register an override in ~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf\n' "$1" >&2
322	        unset _pat; return 3
323	    }
324	    pkill -TERM -f -- "$_pat"
325	    _rc=$?
326	    unset _pat
327	    return "$_rc"
328	}
329	
330	# appactivate NAME — bring to front. Needs window-calls ext for true focus.
331	appactivate() {
332	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
333	        printf 'usage: appactivate <AppName>\n  Bring app to front. With GNOME `window-calls` extension: D-Bus call by WM_CLASS.\n  Without it: falls through to applaunch (single-instance apps re-focus).\n'
334	        return 0 ;;
335	    esac
336	    _linuxapp_guard_linux || return 1
337	    _linuxapp_need_name "$1" appactivate || return 2
338	    _linuxapp_detect_winext
339	    if [ "${_linuxapp_have_winext:-0}" = 1 ]; then
340	        _wc=$(_linuxapp_resolve_wmclass "$1")
341	        if [ -n "$_wc" ]; then
342	            if gdbus call --session \
343	                --dest org.gnome.Shell \
344	                --object-path /org/gnome/Shell/Extensions/Windows \
345	                --method org.gnome.Shell.Extensions.Windows.Activate \
346	                "$_wc" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
347	                unset _wc
348	                return 0
349	            fi
350	        fi
351	        unset _wc
352	    fi
353	    applaunch "$1"
354	}
355	
356	# apprestart NAME — graceful quit + poll-gone (≤15s) + relaunch.
357	# If the app isn't running, this just launches it (mirrors macOS semantics
358	# where `tell app to quit` is silent on a non-running target).
359	apprestart() {
360	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
361	        printf 'usage: apprestart <AppName>\n  appquit + poll until process gone (up to 15s) + applaunch.\n  Launches if not currently running.\n'
362	        return 0 ;;
363	    esac
364	    _linuxapp_guard_linux || return 1
365	    _linuxapp_need_name "$1" apprestart || return 2
366	    if apprunning "$1"; then
367	        appquit "$1" || return $?
368	        _i=0
369	        while [ "$_i" -lt 30 ] && apprunning "$1"; do
370	            sleep 0.5
371	            _i=$((_i + 1))
372	        done
373	        unset _i
374	    fi
375	    applaunch "$1"
376	}
377	
378	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
379	# Public: inspection
380	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
381	
382	# apprunning NAME — silent boolean.
383	apprunning() {
384	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
385	        printf 'usage: apprunning <AppName>\n  Silent. Exit 0 if process matching pattern is found, 1 otherwise.\n'
386	        return 0 ;;
387	    esac
388	    _linuxapp_guard_linux || return 1
389	    _linuxapp_need_name "$1" apprunning || return 2
390	    _pat=$(_linuxapp_resolve_pattern "$1") || { unset _pat; return 1; }
391	    pgrep -f -- "$_pat" >/dev/null 2>&1
392	    _rc=$?
393	    unset _pat
394	    return "$_rc"
395	}
396	
397	_linuxapp_first_pid() {
398	    _pat=$(_linuxapp_resolve_pattern "$1") || { unset _pat; return 1; }
399	    _out=$(pgrep -f -- "$_pat" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
400	    unset _pat
401	    [ -n "$_out" ] || { unset _out; return 1; }
402	    printf '%s\n' "$_out"
403	    unset _out
404	}
405	
406	# applist [--pids|--all] — list registered + auto-derived running apps.
407	applist() {
408	    case "${1:-}" in -h|--help)
409	        printf 'usage: applist [--pids|--all]\n'
410	        printf '  Default     names of running registered+auto-derived apps, one per line.\n'
411	        printf '  --pids      "<pid>\\t<name>" — used by tv linux-apps channel.\n'
412	        printf '  --all       all .desktop entries the helper knows about (running or not),\n'
413	        printf '              with "(running)" annotation.\n'
414	        return 0 ;;
415	    esac
416	    _linuxapp_guard_linux || return 1
417	    _mode=${1:-names}
418	    case "$_mode" in
419	        --pids) _mode=pids ;;
420	        --all)  _mode=all ;;
421	        names)  ;;
422	        *) printf 'applist: unknown option %s\n' "$_mode" >&2; unset _mode; return 2 ;;
423	    esac
424	
425	    # Set of names we've emitted (avoids dupes from both registry + auto scan).
426	    _seen=$(mktemp 2>/dev/null) || _seen=/tmp/applist.$$
427	    : > "$_seen"
428	
429	    # 1. Registered apps. Also write the registered NAME and its resolved
430	    #    desktop-id to $_seen so auto-discovery doesn't emit duplicates.
431	    _linuxapp_keys | while IFS= read -r _n; do
432	        [ -z "$_n" ] && continue
433	        _pid=$(_linuxapp_first_pid "$_n" 2>/dev/null)
434	        printf '%s\n' "$_n" >> "$_seen"
435	        _did=${_linuxapp_desktop[$_n]:-}
436	        [ -n "$_did" ] && printf '%s\n' "$_did" >> "$_seen"
437	        case "$_mode" in
438	            names) [ -n "$_pid" ] && printf '%s\n' "$_n" ;;
439	            pids)  [ -n "$_pid" ] && printf '%s\t%s\n' "$_pid" "$_n" ;;
440	            all)
441	                if [ -n "$_pid" ]; then
442	                    printf '%s\t%s\t(running)\n' "$_pid" "$_n"
443	                else
444	                    printf '\t%s\t\n' "$_n"
445	                fi
446	                ;;
447	        esac
448	    done
449	
450	    # 2. Auto-derive: scan all .desktop stems, pgrep each by FULL Exec path
451	    #    (NOT basename — basename match is too loose and emits false positives
452	    #    for short words like "info" / "idle" / "flatpak"). Trade-off: misses
453	    #    AppImage/snap runtime processes whose actual binary lives at a path
454	    #    different from .desktop Exec — those apps must be explicitly
455	    #    registered. Skip names already emitted from the registry.
456	    for _d in /usr/share/applications "$HOME/.local/share/applications" \
457	              /var/lib/flatpak/exports/share/applications \
458	              "$HOME/.local/share/flatpak/exports/share/applications" \
459	              /var/lib/snapd/desktop/applications; do
460	        [ -d "$_d" ] || continue
461	        for _f in "$_d"/*.desktop; do
462	            [ -f "$_f" ] || continue
463	            _stem=${_f##*/}; _stem=${_stem%.desktop}
464	            if grep -Fxq "$_stem" "$_seen" 2>/dev/null; then continue; fi
465	            _ef=$(awk -F= '/^Exec=/ {sub(/^Exec=/,""); print; exit}' "$_f" 2>/dev/null)
466	            _ec=$(printf '%s' "$_ef" | sed -E 's/[[:space:]]+%[a-zA-Z]+//g')
467	            _ep=${_ec%% *}
468	            # Require absolute path for auto-discovery (rules out wrappers
469	            # like "flatpak run ..." which would match every flatpak app).
470	            case "$_ep" in /*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
471	            _pid=$(pgrep -f -- "$_ep" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
472	            case "$_mode" in
473	                names) [ -n "$_pid" ] && printf '%s\n' "$_stem" ;;
474	                pids)  [ -n "$_pid" ] && printf '%s\t%s\n' "$_pid" "$_stem" ;;
475	                all)
476	                    if [ -n "$_pid" ]; then
477	                        printf '%s\t%s\t(running)\n' "$_pid" "$_stem"
478	                    else
479	                        printf '\t%s\t\n' "$_stem"
480	                    fi
481	                    ;;
482	            esac
483	        done
484	    done
485	
486	    rm -f -- "$_seen"
487	    unset _mode _seen _n _pid _d _f _stem _ef _ec _ep _eb
488	}
489	
490	# appresponsive NAME [TIMEOUT_SEC] — best-effort MPRIS probe.
491	# No public-API analog to macOS Apple Events for non-MPRIS apps.
492	appresponsive() {
493	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
494	        printf 'usage: appresponsive <AppName> [TIMEOUT_SEC]\n'
495	        printf '  Exit 0 if MPRIS probe succeeds within TIMEOUT (default 2s).\n'
496	        printf '  Exit 1 if not running, or MPRIS probe times out.\n'
497	        printf '  Apps without --mpris registered degrade to apprunning + stderr note\n'
498	        printf '  (Linux has no public-API equivalent to macOS Apple Events for\n'
499	        printf '  non-MPRIS apps; Electron/Firefox provide no responsiveness probe).\n'
500	        return 0 ;;
501	    esac
502	    _linuxapp_guard_linux || return 1
503	    _linuxapp_need_name "$1" appresponsive || return 2
504	    apprunning "$1" || return 1
505	    _to=${2:-2}
506	    _mpris=${_linuxapp_mpris[$1]:-}
507	    if [ -n "$_mpris" ] && command -v playerctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
508	        timeout "$_to" playerctl -p "$_mpris" status >/dev/null 2>&1
509	        _rc=$?
510	        unset _to _mpris
511	        return "$_rc"
512	    fi
513	    printf 'appresponsive: %s has no --mpris handle; degrading to apprunning (no public Linux API for non-MPRIS apps)\n' "$1" >&2
514	    unset _to _mpris
515	    return 0
516	}
517	
518	{{ end -}}
519

```text
1	{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
2	# mac-apps channel — macOS GUI app control via Apple Events
3	#
4	# Pick a foreground GUI app, then choose a lifecycle action. Defaults are
5	# safe: Enter brings the app to front; destructive actions are Alt-gated.
6	#
7	# Pairs with: dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl (sourced by every action
8	#             to reuse appactivate / appquit / apprestart / appresponsive)
9	#             dot_config/television/cable/mac-procs.toml.tmpl (process picker,
10	#             sorted by compressed-aware memory — for profiling, not control)
11	#             dot_config/television/cable/kill-process.toml (cross-platform
12	#             process killer; default Enter = SIGTERM, no Apple Events)
13	#
14	# Why a separate channel from mac-procs / kill-process:
15	#   - kill-process Enter = SIGTERM — destructive for apps with state
16	#     (OrbStack VMs, Docker daemons, Slack drafts, unsaved buffers).
17	#   - mac-procs Enter = passthrough — for analysis, not lifecycle.
18	#   - mac-apps Enter = activate — non-destructive default; graceful Quit
19	#     is one Alt-key away and uses Apple Events so apps tear down cleanly.
20	#
21	# Usage:
22	#   tv mac-apps
23	#
24	# Keybindings:
25	#   Enter      Activate (bring to front)
26	#   Alt+Q      Graceful Quit (⌘Q-equivalent Apple Event) + reload
27	#   Alt+R      Quit + poll until gone + relaunch + reload
28	#   Alt+H      Hide app windows (System Events visible=false)
29	#   Alt+K      Force kill by PID (SIGKILL; last resort) + reload
30	#   Alt+I      Info pager: ps + full lsappinfo dump
31	#   Alt+P      Probe responsiveness (5s Apple Event timeout)
32	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview (metadata <-> responsiveness)
33	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
34	#
35	# Why Alt+ rather than Ctrl+: tmux root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows inner
36	# apps. See CLAUDE.md "Keybinding" cross-file rule.
37	
38	[metadata]
39	name = "mac-apps"
40	description = "macOS apps — graceful quit / restart / activate / hide via Apple Events"
41	requirements = []
42	
43	[source]
44	# AppleScript exposes (unix id, name) for foreground GUI apps in one query.
45	# `background only is false` filters out daemons / agents / loginwindow etc.
46	# Output is "<pid>\t<name>\n" — matches `applist --pids` from the shell
47	# helper, but inlined so this channel works even before chezmoi-apply
48	# deploys the helper file.
49	command = """osascript -e 'tell application "System Events"' -e 'set out to ""' -e 'repeat with p in (every application process whose background only is false)' -e 'set out to out & (unix id of p) & tab & (name of p) & linefeed' -e 'end repeat' -e 'return out' -e 'end tell' 2>/dev/null"""
50	display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}"
51	# Default stdout when piping `tv mac-apps | ...` is the app NAME — what
52	# every helper (appquit/applaunch/appactivate/apprestart) wants on argv.
53	output = "{split:\\t:1}"
54	
55	[preview]
56	# Cycle 1: ps + lsappinfo. Fast (<50 ms).
57	# Cycle 2: responsiveness probe. ~2s per render — opt-in via Ctrl+F.
58	command = [
59	  """pid='{split:\\t:0}'
60	ps -p "$pid" -o pid,ppid,user,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,command 2>/dev/null
61	echo
62	lsappinfo info "$pid" 2>/dev/null | head -30""",
63	  """name='{split:\\t:1}'
64	. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh 2>/dev/null
65	printf 'App: %s\\n' "$name"
66	if appresponsive "$name" 2>/dev/null; then
67	  printf 'Status: responsive\\n'
68	else
69	  printf 'Status: NOT responding (or hung)\\n'
70	fi
71	printf '\\n(2s Apple Event timeout — false positives possible during launch)\\n'""",
72	]
73	header = "{split:\\t:1}  (pid {split:\\t:0})"
74	
75	[ui]
76	input_header = "macOS Apps"
77	
78	[keybindings]
79	enter = "actions:activate"
80	alt-q = ["actions:quit", "reload_source"]
81	alt-r = ["actions:restart", "reload_source"]
82	alt-h = "actions:hide"
83	alt-k = ["actions:force-kill", "reload_source"]
84	alt-i = "actions:info"
85	alt-p = "actions:probe"
86	
87	[actions.activate]
88	description = "Bring app to front (Alt+Tab equivalent)"
89	command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && appactivate '{split:\\t:1}'"""
90	mode = "fork"
91	
92	[actions.quit]
93	description = "Graceful Quit (⌘Q-equivalent Apple Event)"
94	command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && appquit '{split:\\t:1}'"""
95	mode = "fork"
96	
97	[actions.restart]
98	description = "Quit + poll until process gone + relaunch"
99	# `execute` (not `fork`) because apprestart polls for up to 15s; we want
100	# the user to see "still quitting…" if it takes a moment.
101	command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && apprestart '{split:\\t:1}'"""
102	mode = "execute"
103	
104	[actions.hide]
105	description = "Hide app windows (System Events visible=false)"
106	# Inlined rather than reusing the helper file because the shell helper
107	# doesn't expose `hide` as a function — only the four lifecycle verbs.
108	command = """osascript -e 'on run argv' -e 'tell application "System Events" to set visible of (first process whose name is (item 1 of argv)) to false' -e 'end run' -- '{split:\\t:1}'"""
109	mode = "fork"
110	
111	[actions.force-kill]
112	description = "SIGKILL by PID (last resort; bypasses Apple Event)"
113	# Uses PID column, not name. Apps with multiple processes (Chrome Helper,
114	# Electron renderers) only have their main process listed in `applist`,
115	# so SIGKILL here kills the parent — children are reaped by launchd.
116	command = "kill -9 '{split:\\t:0}'"
117	mode = "fork"
118	
119	[actions.info]
120	description = "Detail pager: ps + full lsappinfo"
121	command = """pid='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:1}'; { printf '=== %s (pid %s) ===\\n\\n' "$name" "$pid"; ps -p "$pid" -o pid,ppid,user,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,command; printf '\\n'; lsappinfo info "$pid"; } 2>/dev/null | less -R; printf '\\n[Press Enter to exit]\\n'; read -r _"""
122	mode = "execute"
123	
124	[actions.probe]
125	description = "Probe app responsiveness (5s Apple Event timeout)"
126	command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && name='{split:\\t:1}' && (appresponsive "$name" 5 && printf '%s: responsive\\n' "$name" || printf '%s: NOT responding\\n' "$name"); sleep 2"""
127	mode = "execute"
128	{{ end -}}
129
```

1	{{- if and (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") (eq .profile "ubuntu_desktop") -}}
2	# linux-apps channel — Linux GUI app control via gtk-launch + pkill -TERM
3	#
4	# Linux counterpart to dot_config/television/cable/mac-apps.toml.tmpl.
5	# Pick a running GUI app (registered or auto-derived from .desktop scan),
6	# then choose a lifecycle action. Same keybindings as mac-apps where the
7	# verb exists on both sides — Alt+H is mac-only by design (Linux can't
8	# hide windows without compositor IPC).
9	#
10	# Pairs with: dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl (sourced by every
11	#             action to reuse appactivate / appquit / apprestart /
12	#             appresponsive — and by [source] to drive `applist --pids`)
13	#             ~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf (user override file; lets
14	#             users register per-app pkill patterns for AppImage/snap/
15	#             Flatpak apps that auto-derivation can't resolve correctly)
16	#
17	# Coverage caveats (mirrors backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md):
18	#   - appactivate falls back to applaunch unless the GNOME window-calls
19	#     extension is installed; documented as best-effort.
20	#   - appresponsive only meaningful for apps registered with --mpris=NAME
21	#     (Spotify, mpv, VLC, …); for Electron/Firefox apps it degrades to
22	#     apprunning + stderr note. No public Linux API analog to macOS
23	#     Apple Events' `with timeout`.
24	#
25	# Usage:
26	#   tv linux-apps
27	#
28	# Keybindings:
29	#   Enter      Activate (bring to front — best-effort without window-calls)
30	#   Alt+Q      Graceful Quit (pkill -TERM via app's pkill pattern) + reload
31	#   Alt+R      Quit + poll until process gone + relaunch + reload
32	#   Alt+K      Force kill by PID (SIGKILL; last resort) + reload
33	#   Alt+I      Info pager: ps + pgrep details
34	#   Alt+P      Probe responsiveness (MPRIS-only; stderr note otherwise)
35	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview (metadata <-> responsiveness)
36	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
37	#
38	# Why Alt+ rather than Ctrl+: tmux root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows inner
39	# apps. See CLAUDE.md "Keybinding" cross-file rule.
40	
41	[metadata]
42	name = "linux-apps"
43	description = "Linux apps — graceful quit / restart / activate via gtk-launch + pkill"
44	requirements = []
45	
46	[source]
47	# Source the helper (which also sources ~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf
48	# to populate the user's overrides), then emit `<pid>\t<name>` for each
49	# running app the helper recognises. Output format matches mac-apps for
50	# preview / display / output split consistency.
51	command = """sh -c '. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh 2>/dev/null && applist --pids' 2>/dev/null"""
52	display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}"
53	# Default stdout when piping `tv linux-apps | ...` is the app NAME — what
54	# every helper (appquit/applaunch/appactivate/apprestart) wants on argv.
55	output = "{split:\\t:1}"
56	
57	[preview]
58	# Cycle 1: ps + pgrep tree. Fast (<50 ms).
59	# Cycle 2: responsiveness probe — MPRIS-only meaningful response.
60	command = [
61	  """pid='{split:\\t:0}'
62	name='{split:\\t:1}'
63	ps -p "$pid" -o pid,ppid,user,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,comm 2>/dev/null
64	echo

1	"""yth search — FTS5 search over watch history.
2	
3	Default matches title / channel / description (ranked title≫channel≫desc via
4	bm25). ``--subs`` additionally matches indexed caption text and shows a
5	snippet. ``--json`` emits structured results for piping. DB-only.
6	
7	The tv channel (`tv yth`) only fuzzy-filters the metadata *display string* —
8	television's source is single-shot and never sees the live query — so deep
9	caption search lives here, in the CLI.
10	"""
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	import json
14	import sys
15	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
16	from typing import Annotated
17	
18	import tyro
19	from rich.console import Console
20	from rich.table import Table
21	
22	from scripts.yth import connect, fts_query, short_date
23	
24	
25	@dataclass
26	class Args:
27	    query: Annotated[
28	        list[str],
29	        tyro.conf.Positional,
30	        tyro.conf.arg(help="Search terms (ANDed). Quote to include spaces."),
31	    ] = field(default_factory=list)
32	    subs: Annotated[
33	        bool, tyro.conf.arg(help="Also search indexed caption text.")
34	    ] = False
35	    json_out: Annotated[
36	        bool, tyro.conf.arg(name="json", help="Emit JSON instead of a table.")
37	    ] = False
38	    limit: Annotated[int, tyro.conf.arg(help="Max results.")] = 50
39	    raw: Annotated[
40	        bool,
41	        tyro.conf.arg(help="Pass the query straight to FTS5 (native MATCH syntax)."),
42	    ] = False
43	
44	
45	def _meta_hits(con, match: str, limit: int):
46	    return con.execute(
47	        """
48	        SELECT v.video_id, v.title, v.channel, s.watch_count, s.last_watched
49	        FROM videos_fts f
50	        JOIN videos v ON v.id = f.rowid
51	        LEFT JOIN video_stats s ON s.video_id = v.video_id
52	        WHERE videos_fts MATCH ?
53	        ORDER BY bm25(videos_fts, 8.0, 4.0, 1.0)
54	        LIMIT ?
55	        """,
56	        (match, limit),
57	    ).fetchall()
58	
59	
60	def _subs_hits(con, match: str, limit: int):
61	    return con.execute(
62	        """
63	        SELECT sub.video_id, v.title, v.channel, s.watch_count, s.last_watched,
64	               snippet(subtitles_fts, 0, '»', '«', '…', 10) AS snip
65	        FROM subtitles_fts sf
66	        JOIN subtitles sub ON sub.id = sf.rowid
67	        JOIN videos v ON v.video_id = sub.video_id
68	        LEFT JOIN video_stats s ON s.video_id = v.video_id
69	        WHERE subtitles_fts MATCH ?
70	        ORDER BY bm25(subtitles_fts)
71	        LIMIT ?
72	        """,
73	        (match, limit),
74	    ).fetchall()
75	
76	
77	def cli(args: Args) -> int:
78	    text = " ".join(args.query).strip()
79	    if not text:
80	        print("yth search: empty query. Try: yth search <terms>", file=sys.stderr)
81	        return 2
82	
83	    match = text if args.raw else fts_query(text)
84	    if not match:
85	        print("yth search: query has no searchable terms.", file=sys.stderr)
86	        return 2
87	
88	    con = connect()
89	    import sqlite3
90	
91	    try:
92	        meta = _meta_hits(con, match, args.limit)
93	        subs = _subs_hits(con, match, args.limit) if args.subs else []
94	    except sqlite3.OperationalError as e:
95	        print(
96	            f"yth search: FTS5 rejected the query ({e}).\n"
97	            "  Drop --raw, or quote special characters.",
98	            file=sys.stderr,
99	        )
100	        return 2
101	
102	    # Merge: metadata hits keep their rank; caption-only hits append. A video
103	    # matched by both is tagged with both sources.
104	    order: list[str] = []
105	    by_id: dict[str, dict] = {}
106	    for r in meta:
107	        by_id[r["video_id"]] = {
108	            "video_id": r["video_id"],
109	            "title": r["title"] or r["video_id"],
110	            "channel": r["channel"] or "-",
111	            "watch_count": r["watch_count"] or 0,
112	            "last_watched": r["last_watched"],
113	            "matched": ["meta"],
114	            "snippet": None,
115	        }
116	        order.append(r["video_id"])
117	    for r in subs:
118	        vid = r["video_id"]
119	        if vid in by_id:
120	            by_id[vid]["matched"].append("subs")
121	            by_id[vid]["snippet"] = r["snip"]
122	        else:
123	            by_id[vid] = {
124	                "video_id": vid,
125	                "title": r["title"] or vid,
126	                "channel": r["channel"] or "-",
127	                "watch_count": r["watch_count"] or 0,
128	                "last_watched": r["last_watched"],
129	                "matched": ["subs"],
130	                "snippet": r["snip"],
131	            }
132	            order.append(vid)
133	
134	    results = [by_id[v] for v in order]
135	
136	    if args.json_out:
137	        print(json.dumps(results, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
138	        return 0
139	
140	    if not results:
141	        print(f"yth search: no matches for {text!r}", file=sys.stderr)
142	        return 0
143	
144	    table = Table(show_lines=False, header_style="bold")
145	    cols = ["watched", "channel", "title", "match", "id"]
146	    if args.subs:
147	        cols.insert(4, "caption")
148	    for header in cols:
149	        table.add_column(header)
150	    for r in results:
151	        cells = [
152	            short_date(r["last_watched"]),
153	            r["channel"][:26],
154	            r["title"][:60],
155	            "+".join(r["matched"]),
156	        ]
157	        if args.subs:
158	            cells.append((r["snippet"] or "")[:60])
159	        cells.append(r["video_id"])
160	        table.add_row(*cells)
161	    Console().print(table)
162	    return 0
163	
164	
165	def main() -> int:
166	    return cli(tyro.cli(Args, prog="yth search"))
167	
168	
169	if __name__ == "__main__":

 `./scripts/yth/list.py`

```text
1	"""yth list — dump watch history, newest first.
2	
3	Default output is a rich.Table for terminal browsing. ``--tsv`` emits the
4	tab-separated layout the `tv yth` channel consumes as its source (column 0 =
5	video_id, which tv hands to the preview + action commands).
6	
7	DB-only: never imports yt_dlp, so it stays instant as a tv source.
8	"""
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import sys
12	from dataclasses import dataclass
13	from typing import Annotated
14	
15	import tyro
16	from rich.console import Console
17	from rich.table import Table
18	
19	from scripts.yth import connect, fmt_duration, short_date
20	
21	# tv wants the whole history in one shot; it does the fuzzy filtering itself.
22	# 20k rows is trivial for television; the cap is a runaway guard only.
23	_TSV_CAP = 20000
24	_TABLE_CAP = 200
25	
26	
27	@dataclass
28	class Args:
29	    tsv: Annotated[
30	        bool,
31	        tyro.conf.arg(help="Emit TSV for the `tv yth` source instead of a table."),
32	    ] = False
33	    limit: Annotated[
34	        int,
35	        tyro.conf.arg(help="Max rows (-1 = auto: 20000 for --tsv, 200 for the table)."),
36	    ] = -1
37	
38	
39	def _rows(con, limit: int):
40	    return con.execute(
41	        """
42	        SELECT v.video_id, v.title, v.channel, v.duration,
43	               s.watch_count, s.last_watched
44	        FROM videos v
45	        LEFT JOIN video_stats s ON s.video_id = v.video_id
46	        ORDER BY (s.last_watched IS NULL), s.last_watched DESC, v.id DESC
47	        LIMIT ?
48	        """,
49	        (limit,),
50	    ).fetchall()
51	
52	
53	def _clean(value) -> str:
54	    """Scrub tab/newline so a cell can't break the TSV column framing."""
55	    return str(value or "").replace("\t", " ").replace("\r", " ").replace("\n", " ").strip()
56	
57	
58	def _marker(watch_count) -> str:
59	    n = watch_count or 1
60	    return "▶" if n <= 1 else f"×{n}"
61	
62	
63	def cli(args: Args) -> int:
64	    con = connect()
65	    if args.limit >= 0:
66	        limit = args.limit
67	    else:
68	        limit = _TSV_CAP if args.tsv else _TABLE_CAP
69	    rows = _rows(con, limit)
70	
71	    if args.tsv:
72	        out = []
73	        for r in rows:
74	            out.append(
75	                "\t".join(
76	                    (
77	                        r["video_id"],
78	                        _marker(r["watch_count"]),
79	                        _clean(r["channel"]) or "-",
80	                        _clean(r["title"]) or r["video_id"],
81	                        short_date(r["last_watched"]),
82	                        fmt_duration(r["duration"]),
83	                    )
84	                )

188	def _parse_iso(ts: str | None) -> datetime | None:
189	    if not ts:
190	        return None
191	    m = _ISO_PAT.match(ts)
192	    if not m:
193	        return None
194	    head, tz = m.group(1), m.group(2)
195	    if not tz:
196	        normalised = head
197	    elif tz == "Z":
198	        normalised = head + "+00:00"
199	    elif re.match(r"^[+-]\d{4}$", tz):
200	        normalised = head + f"{tz[:3]}:{tz[3:]}"
201	    else:
202	        normalised = head + tz
203	    try:
204	        return datetime.fromisoformat(normalised)
205	    except ValueError:
206	        return None

```text
1	# Zsh & Bash Completions
2	
3	How tab completions are organized in this dotfiles project — for both upstream tools and in-house CLIs (`fleet`, `mlf`, `pqsum`, `mi-router`, `x`).
4	
5	## How autocomplete works (mechanics)
6	
7	Tab completion is the same idea on both shells but the plumbing differs.
8	
9	### zsh — `compinit` + `fpath` + autoload `_<tool>` functions
10	
11	1. **`compinit`** scans every directory in `$fpath` for files starting with `_` and registers them as completion candidates. Run by oh-my-zsh once at startup.
12	2. **`$fpath`** is zsh's function search path. Order in this repo (`dot_zshrc.tmpl:67-70`):
13	   ```
14	   ~/.zfunc                                             ← user-generated (this repo's lazy autoload target)
15	   ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/     ← community (184 tools)
16	   ~/.docker/completions/                               ← Docker-shipped
17	   $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/           ← Homebrew-managed
18	   ```
19	3. **The first line of each file** matters: `#compdef <name>` tells zsh which command to bind to. If you write `#compdef fleet`, then `fleet<TAB>` invokes the file's `_fleet` function.
20	4. **Autoload vs eager-load**: a file in `$fpath` is *parsed* the first time the user actually TABs the command (lazy). Files sourced explicitly at startup (e.g. via `load_modular_dir` in this repo) call `compdef _<func> <cmd>` directly — parsed eagerly, no need to be in `$fpath`.
21	5. **`_arguments` DSL** (zsh-only) lets you describe options + positional args declaratively: `'--hosts=[help text]:hosts:_fleet_hosts_csv'` defines the flag, hint, and a custom completer function. See `dot_config/zsh/tools/45_fleet_completion.zsh`.
22	
23	### bash — `bash-completion v2` + `complete -F` + `COMPREPLY`
24	
25	1. **bash-completion v2** is sourced at shell startup by `dot_config/bash/03_completion.bash`. It auto-loads completion files on first TAB.
26	2. **The user dir** is `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/` — drop a file named after the command (e.g. `mi-router`) here and v2 lazy-loads it on TAB.
27	3. **`complete -F _func cmd`** registers a bash function as the completer for `cmd`. The function reads `$COMP_WORDS` / `$COMP_CWORD` and writes candidates to `$COMPREPLY`.
28	4. **`_init_completion` + `compgen`** are bash-completion v2 helpers — `_init_completion` populates `cur`/`prev`/`words`/`cword`; `compgen -W "list" -- "$cur"` filters a wordlist by the current prefix.
29	5. **Eager vs lazy** mirrors zsh: a file in the user dir is lazy; a file sourced via `load_modular_dir` (this repo's `dot_config/bash/`) calls `complete -F` immediately.
30	
31	### Three generation strategies in this repo
32	
33	| Strategy | Where the file lives | Trigger | Best for |
34	|---|---|---|---|
35	| **A. Lazy autoload** | zsh `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` / bash `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` | First TAB on the command | Tools that ship `--print-completion <shell>` or similar (tyro, click, clap-derive — including this repo's `mi-router`) |
36	| **B. Eager-load at startup** | `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<tool>_completion.bash` | Sourced via `load_modular_dir` after compinit / bash-completion v2 init | Hand-written completion (this repo's `fleet`, `mlf`, `pqsum`, `x`) |
37	| **C. Cached eval at startup** | `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/<shell>/<tool>_completion.<ext>` | Sourced via shell `init` script (`dot_config/shell/<NN>_<tool>.sh`) | Slow generators whose output has side effects beyond `compdef` (e.g. `thefuck --alias` outputs an `alias` line — needs to land in the running shell's namespace, not just a deferred `_<tool>` function) |
38	
39	Cache invalidation in classes A and C uses **binary-mtime check**:
40	```sh
41	[ ! -f "$cache" ] || [ "$(command -v <tool>)" -nt "$cache" ]  # → regenerate
42	```
43	This catches `brew upgrade`, `uv tool upgrade`, `mise install <NEW>` — anything that bumps the binary's mtime. Manual `<tool>-update-completion` helpers (in `dot_config/{shell,zsh}/10_aliases.zsh`) cover edge cases (gem-only upgrades, in-place replacements, cache corruption).
44	
45	## Architecture
46	
47	```
48	compinit runs once (inside oh-my-zsh.sh)
49	        │
50	        ├── ~/.zfunc/                          ← user-generated completions (NOT tracked by chezmoi)
51	        ├── ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/       ← community completions (184 files, cloned by ansible)
52	        │     └── zsh-completions/src/
53	        ├── ~/.docker/completions/             ← Docker-shipped completions
54	        ├── $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/        ← Homebrew-managed completions (via `brew completions link`)
55	        │     └── site-functions/
56	        └── $ZSH/completions/                  ← oh-my-zsh built-in completions
57	```
58	
59	All `fpath` additions are in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` **before** `source "$ZSH/oh-my-zsh.sh"`, so `compinit` runs exactly once and picks up everything.
60	
61	## Completion Categories
62	
63	Tools fall into four categories:
64	
65	### A. Self-generating (`tool completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_tool`)
66	
67	Most modern CLI tools can output their own completion script. **Auto-generated for both shells** by the `chezmoi apply` hook (`run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl` → `scripts/generate_completions.sh`); see [Generating Completions After Fresh Install](#generating-completions-after-fresh-install) for opt-out + manual rerun.
68	
69	| Tool | Command |
70	|------|---------|
71	| `uv` | `uv generate-shell-completion zsh` |
72	| `mise` | `mise completion zsh` |
73	| `chezmoi` | `chezmoi completion zsh` |
74	| `just` | `just --completions zsh` |
75	| `bat` | `bat --completion zsh` |
76	| `delta` | `delta --generate-completion zsh` |
77	| `starship` | `starship completions zsh` |
78	| `rg` | `rg --generate complete-zsh` |
79	| `fd` | `fd --gen-completions zsh` |
80	| `zellij` | `zellij setup --generate-completion zsh` |
81	| `sesh` | `sesh completion zsh` |
82	| `pueue` | `pueue completions zsh` |
83	| `docker` | `docker completion zsh` |
84	| `gh` | `gh completion -s zsh` |
85	| `opencode` | `opencode completion zsh` |
86	| `bw` | `bw completion --shell zsh` |
87	
88	**Usage pattern:**
89	
90	```bash
91	# Generate once (or after upgrade)
92	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc
93	uv generate-shell-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_uv
94	mise completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_mise
95	```
96	
97	### B. Pre-bundled (no action needed)
98	
99	Completions ship with the package or via the `zsh-completions` community plugin.
100	
101	| Tool | Source |
102	|------|--------|
103	| `eza` | Homebrew formula installs `_eza` into site-functions |
104	| `git` | oh-my-zsh `git` plugin |
105	| `yazi` | Ships `_yazi` in release assets (also in zsh-completions) |
106	| `lazygit` | No completion support; not needed (TUI app) |
107	| `btop` | No completion support; not needed (TUI app) |
108	| Many others | `zsh-completions` plugin covers 184 tools |
109	
110	### C. Eval/source at startup (shell integration)
111	
112	These tools inject completions as part of broader shell integration. Most live in the POSIX `dot_config/shell/` layer (sourced by both zsh and bash); zsh-only ones live in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`.
113	
114	| Tool | Where | How | Cached? |
115	|------|-------|-----|---------|
116	| `fzf` | `dot_config/shell/10_fzf.sh` | `eval "$(fzf --zsh)"` (zsh) / `eval "$(fzf --bash)"` (bash) | — |
117	| `zoxide` | `dot_config/shell/20_zoxide.sh` | `eval "$(zoxide init <shell>)"` | — |
118	| `direnv` | `dot_config/shell/30_direnv.sh` | `eval "$(direnv hook <shell>)"` | — |
119	| `marimo` | `dot_config/shell/29_marimo.sh` | `_MARIMO_COMPLETE=<shell>_source marimo` | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/{zsh,bash}/marimo_completion.{zsh,bash}` — refresh via `marimo-update-completion` |
120	| `thefuck` | `dot_config/shell/27_thefuck.sh` | `thefuck --alias` | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/{zsh,bash}/thefuck_alias.{zsh,bash}` — refresh via `thefuck-update-completion` |
121	| `try-cli` | `dot_config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh` | `ruby try.rb init` (zsh-only) | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/zsh/try_init.zsh` — refresh via `try-update-completion` |
122	
123	> **Cached entries** auto-invalidate when the tool's binary mtime is newer than the cache file (`[ "$(command -v <tool>)" -nt "$cache" ]`) — catches `mise install <NEW>`, `brew upgrade`, `uv tool upgrade`. Manual refresh helpers handle edge cases: gem-only upgrades that don't bump the ruby binary, in-place tool replacements, or cache corruption. The pattern mirrors `dot_config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` (the canonical example).
124	
125	### D. No completion support
126	
127	`claude`, `gemini`, `agy`/`agyc` (Antigravity CLI), `btop`, `lazygit` -- no generation command available.
128	
129	### E. Python tools via `shtab` / `tyro` / `click` / `argcomplete`
130	
131	Python CLI frameworks can generate completions. Pick by what your script uses:
132	
133	- **[tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/tab_completion/)** (this repo's `mi-router` + every `scripts/fleet/*.py` and `scripts/mlf/*.py` subcommand): `<tool> --tyro-write-completion zsh <path>`. Native flag — auto-added when you call `tyro.cli(...)`. tyro emits `#compdef <full-binary-path>` for zsh, so post-process the first line to the short name (see `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` for the canonical pattern). Bash output already binds `basename`, no fixup needed.
134	- **[shtab](https://github.com/iterative/shtab)**: `shtab --shell=zsh my_module.parser > ~/.zfunc/_my_tool`. Decorate-an-`argparse.ArgumentParser` style; works for both shells.
135	- **argcomplete**: `register-python-argcomplete tool_name` (eval-at-startup style, category C). Requires the script to call `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` before `parse_args()`. Cross-shell.
136	- **click** (used by `marimo`, `thefuck`, `mlflow`, `litellm`, etc.): `_TOOL_COMPLETE=zsh_source tool > ~/.zfunc/_tool`. The completion script may include side effects (aliases / functions) — if so, treat as category C and cache via `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/<shell>/<tool>_completion.<ext>`. See the canonical pattern at `dot_config/shell/29_marimo.sh`.
137	
138	> **TAB display itself**, not just completion data: see [`oh-my-zsh-plugins.md`](oh-my-zsh-plugins.md) "TAB display upgrades — alternatives evaluated" for fzf-tab (recommended) and rejected alternatives (zsh-autocomplete / carapace-bin / inshellisense).

160	**Dynamic candidates wired up:**
161	
162	- `fleet` host names — `_fleet_hosts_one` / `_fleet_hosts_csv` shell out to `fleet hosts --list`. Used for the positional `fleet hosts NAME`, `fleet chezmoi diff HOST`, `fleet chezmoi tail HOST`, and the `--hosts=foo,bar,baz` CSV flag everywhere.
163	- `pqsum -g <GROUP>` — `_pqsum` shells out to `pueue status --json | jq '.groups | keys[]'`.
164	- `mlf` ids (run-id, experiment-id, model-name) — **not** auto-completed (would round-trip MLflow tracking server, possibly auth-required). Use `tv mlflow` for fuzzy id picking instead.
165	- `yth` video ids — **not** auto-completed (opaque 11-char ids; enumerating the whole history on every TAB is wasteful). Use `tv yth` or `yth search <query>` instead.
166	- `wake` host names — `_wake` shells out to `wake --list-names` (reads `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`), same pattern as `_fleet_hosts_one`.
167	
168	**Adding a new in-house CLI** (decision flow):
169	
170	1. **Does it use tyro?** → Use Strategy A. Mirror `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh`. Add a `<tool>-update-completion` helper to `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`. Don't forget to rewrite `#compdef` in zsh post-gen.
171	2. **Does it use argparse?** → Two sub-options:
172	   - Add `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` to the script + Strategy C cached eval at startup.
173	   - Hand-write Strategy B completion (smaller / no Python dependency at every shell startup).
174	3. **Hand-rolled / shell script** → Strategy B hand-written. One zsh file in `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`, one bash file in `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`. Mirror `_fleet`'s structure: top-level dispatcher → per-subcommand functions → dynamic helpers.
175	4. **Update this table + `docs/shells/aliases.md`** in the same commit (per the cross-file maintenance rule in `CLAUDE.md`).
176	
177	## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi
178	
179	**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:
180	
181	1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
182	2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
183	3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
184	4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.
185	
186	### What we DO track
187	
188	- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
189	- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
190	- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
191	- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`
192	
193	## Generating Completions After Fresh Install
194	
195	**Automatic — no manual step needed.** Every `chezmoi apply` runs `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl`, which calls `scripts/generate_completions.sh` and regenerates completion for the 14 self-generating tools listed in Section A (`chezmoi`, `mise`, `uv`, `just`, `starship`, `gh`, `docker`, `rg`, `fd`, `bat`, `delta`, `zellij`, `pueue`, `opencode`).
196	
197	The hook is **idempotent** — it stat-checks each tool's binary mtime against the existing completion file and skips if the cache is fresh. Cost when nothing changed: **~21ms** total (presence checks + 28 stat calls). After an `ansible-playbook` / `brew upgrade` / `mise install <NEW>` that bumps a binary's mtime: ~140ms one-shot to regenerate the affected completions.
198	
199	Output paths:
200	- **zsh**: `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` — lazy-loaded by compinit on first TAB (in `$fpath` via `dot_zshrc.tmpl:68`).
201	- **bash**: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` — lazy-loaded by bash-completion v2 on first TAB.
202	
203	### Manual rerun
204	
205	```bash
206	just completions-refresh                              # force regen all (--force)
207	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh --force          # same, no `just`
208	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh                  # mtime-checked (same as the chezmoi hook)
209	```
210	
211	Use `just completions-refresh` after a tool upgrade outside the chezmoi flow (e.g. `cargo install <tool>`), or to recover from a corrupted completion file.
212	
213	### Opt out
214	
215	```bash
216	export CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN=1   # in ~/.shellrc.adhoc; suppresses the chezmoi-apply hook
217	```
218	
219	Existing completion files stay as-is; you can still run `just completions-refresh` manually.
220	
221	### Add a new tool to the auto-gen inventory
222	
223	Edit the `regen <tool> "<zsh-args>" "<bash-args>"` block in `scripts/generate_completions.sh`. The arguments are whatever follows the tool name to produce the per-shell completion script — check `<tool> completion --help` or `<tool> --help | grep -i complet`. Examples already in the script cover click (`_TOOL_COMPLETE=`), clap (`--generate complete-<shell>`), tyro (`--tyro-write-completion <shell>`-equivalent), cobra (`completion <shell>`), and ad-hoc styles (`--completions <shell>`).
224	
225	### What about tools NOT in the auto-gen inventory?
226	
227	- **`sesh` / `tv` / `worktrunk`**: shell-startup mtime check (each tool has its own `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>.zsh` file that runs the version check on every shell start — these tools are typically `cargo install`-ed outside chezmoi, so they need the per-startup probe to catch user upgrades).
228	- **`bw` / `marimo` / `thefuck` / `try-cli`**: cached eval at startup (their completion script has side effects beyond `compdef`, so the file is `source`'d into the running shell rather than autoloaded).
229	- **`mi-router`**: tyro self-gen, lives in `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` (not the bulk script — has its own `#compdef` rewrite for tyro's full-path output quirk).
230	- **`fleet` / `mlf` / `pqsum` / `x` / `dotcfg` / `agent-warmup`**: hand-written completion in `dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/45-54_*_completion.*` (in-house CLIs without a built-in completion generator). `dotcfg`'s `--set` key list mirrors the PROMPTS table in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`.
231	
232	## Priority / Override Order
233	
234	When the same `_tool` file exists in multiple fpath directories, the **first match wins**:
235	
236	```
237	1. ~/.zfunc/                                    (highest - your overrides)
238	2. ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/
239	3. ~/.docker/completions/
240	4. $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/   (Homebrew-managed)
241	5. /usr/share/zsh/*/functions/                  (system, lowest)
242	```
243	
244	Current `dot_zshrc.tmpl` order:
245	
246	```zsh
247	fpath+=~/.zfunc                     # appended (lowest of custom)
248	fpath=(zsh-completions/src $fpath)  # prepended (higher than ~/.zfunc)
249	fpath=(~/.docker/completions $fpath) # prepended (highest of custom)
250	```
251	
252	If you want `~/.zfunc/` to override community completions, change to prepend:
253	
254	```zsh
255	fpath=(~/.zfunc $fpath)  # prepend instead of append
256	```
257	
258	## FAQ
259	
260	**Q: Should I generate completions for tools that `zsh-completions` already covers?**
261	A: Only if you want the latest version. The community plugin may lag behind. For fast-moving tools (uv, mise), generating your own is worthwhile.
262	
263	**Q: A completion file throws errors after I uninstall a tool. What do I do?**
264	A: Remove the file: `rm ~/.zfunc/_toolname`. Stale `_tool` files in fpath are harmless (silently ignored) unless they have syntax errors.
265	
266	**Q: How do I debug completion issues?**
267	A: Run `echo $fpath | tr ' ' '\n'` to see all fpath entries. Use `which _toolname` to see which completion file is being used. Force rebuild with `rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit`.
268

README.md:127:> CentOS 7 also blocks Linuxbrew install because system curl 7.29 is older than Homebrew's 7.41 minimum, and Homebrew bottles built on Ubuntu 22.04+ don't run on glibc 2.17 anyway. Linuxbrew is fully optional on Linux — every ansible task that uses it has a non-brew fallback (cargo / GitHub musl release / AppImage). On CentOS 7, drop a stub `~/.local/bin/brew` (`#!/bin/sh\nexit 0`) before applying to short-circuit the bootstrap's brew step.
README.md:322:- **GUI Apps on Linux** (`gui_apps` tag on `ubuntu_desktop`): [`gui_apps_linux`](dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) bundles Alacritty (cargo), AppImageLauncher (PPA with `.deb` fallback, Lite variant for noRoot), VSCode (Microsoft apt repo), Cursor (`.deb`), Discord (Flatpak default or `.deb`), optional Steam via Valve apt repo when `installGamingApps=true`, Zen Browser (AppImage + `.desktop` entry for launcher search), and `libfuse2` for AppImage compatibility. macOS equivalents ship via [`Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`](dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl) (Arc + Discord + optional Steam casks there). See [docs/tools/appimage.md](docs/tools/appimage.md) for AppImageLauncher install paths, `ail-cli` usage, and Ubuntu 24.04 AppArmor gotchas.
CLAUDE.md:33:| `app-*` helpers — `dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl` (macOS) ↔ `dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` (Linux) ↔ `dot_config/television/cable/mac-apps.toml.tmpl` ↔ `dot_config/television/cable/linux-apps.toml.tmpl` | Both shell helpers MUST expose the SAME public verb names (`appquit` / `applaunch` / `appactivate` / `apprestart` / `apprunning` / `applist` / `appresponsive`) so users get cross-platform muscle memory. Backends diverge by necessity (Apple Events vs `gtk-launch` + `pkill -TERM` + optional GNOME `window-calls` ext). Adding a new verb to one side: decide whether it can also be implemented on the other; if not, document the gap in `backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md` "Open follow-ups". Both `tv` channel files MUST share Alt-key bindings where the verb exists on both sides — **Alt+H is mac-only by design** (Linux can't hide windows without compositor IPC; the Alt+H slot stays free on `tv linux-apps`). Per-app overrides for Linux AppImage/Snap/Flatpak runtime paths live in `~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf` (not auto-stubbed, matches `.shellrc.secrets` rule) — never auto-generate this file from the helper. | [docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md](docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md) "Controlling installed apps from the shell" section; [pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md](pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md), [pitfalls/linux-app-control-gapplication-zero-coverage.md](pitfalls/linux-app-control-gapplication-zero-coverage.md). Empirical baseline: `gapplication list-apps` returns only ~13 GNOME-core apps on Ubuntu 24.04 Wayland — third-party Electron/AppImage/Snap/Flatpak coverage is **zero**, so don't reach for `gapplication action … quit` as the primary mechanism. |

backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md:16:**Shipped pivot**: hybrid `gtk-launch` + `pkill -TERM` + optional GNOME `window-calls` extension, with a per-user override file for AppImage / Snap / Flatpak runtime-path corrections. 5 of 7 macOS verbs translate cleanly; 1 (`appactivate`) degrades to best-effort without the extension; 1 (`appresponsive`) is MPRIS-only.
backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md:23:2. **AppImage runtime path ≠ `.desktop` `Exec=` path.** Zen's `.desktop` says `~/Applications/zen-x86_64_*.AppImage`; the actual running process is at `/tmp/.mount_remp*/zen`. `pkill -f <Exec-path>` only hits the launcher wrapper, not the real binary. See `pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md`.
backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md:24:3. **`.desktop` cruft is the norm, not the exception.** Zen had 4 `.desktop` entries (3 AppImage residues + 1 custom userapp). Cursor had 2 (apt at `/usr/share/cursor/cursor` + AppImage). Discord had 2 (apt + Flatpak — both installed, only apt actually running).
backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md:44:**Override file** (`~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf`, not auto-stubbed): `linux_app_register NAME --desktop=ID --pkill=REGEX --wm-class=CLASS [--mpris=NAME]`. Required for AppImage / Snap / Flatpak apps; recommended where multiple `.desktop` entries exist for one app. See the playbook for the user's 5-app starter snippet.

1	"""mlf — shared helpers for the MLflow umbrella CLI.
2	
3	The umbrella binary (`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mlf`) plus subcommand
4	modules (`scripts/mlf/plot.py`, `list.py`, `download.py`) all share this
5	namespace. Helpers live here instead of being duplicated per-module.
6	
7	`MlflowClient` is constructed lazily (on first call) — importing mlflow is
8	~1s warm, so subcommands that don't need a client (e.g. `mlf -h`,
9	`mlf tv`) don't pay the cost.
10	"""
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	import os
14	import re
15	import shutil
16	import subprocess
17	import sys
18	import warnings
19	from datetime import datetime, timezone
20	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
21	
22	# Fail fast on unreachable HTTP backends. Matches the env defaults used by
23	# the tv-channel helpers (executable_mlflow-source.py / executable_mlflow-
24	# preview.py) so a typo'd MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI surfaces in seconds, not
25	# minutes. mlflow defaults are 120s timeout × 5 retries.
26	os.environ.setdefault("PYTHONWARNINGS", "ignore")
27	os.environ.setdefault("MLFLOW_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT", "5")
28	os.environ.setdefault("MLFLOW_HTTP_REQUEST_MAX_RETRIES", "1")
29	warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

31	if TYPE_CHECKING:
32	    from mlflow.tracking import MlflowClient
33	
34	# 32-char lowercase hex = mlflow run_id. Anchored — partial hex strings
35	# (e.g. an 8-char short id from a copy-paste) don't match.
36	RUN_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{32}$")
37	
38	
39	def make_client() -> "MlflowClient":
40	    """Build a MlflowClient. Imports lazily; silences mlflow's INFO logs.
41	
42	    `logging.getLogger("mlflow").setLevel(WARNING)` MUST run AFTER
43	    `import mlflow` — mlflow.utils.logging_utils installs handlers at
44	    import time and pre-import setLevel calls get overwritten.
45	    """
46	    import logging
47	
48	    # `from mlflow.tracking import MlflowClient` loads the top-level mlflow
49	    # package as a side-effect, which is when mlflow.utils.logging_utils
50	    # installs its INFO-level handlers. The setLevel call below MUST run
51	    # after that, not before — pre-import setLevel gets overwritten.
52	    from mlflow.tracking import MlflowClient
53	
54	    logging.getLogger("mlflow").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
55	    logging.getLogger("alembic").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
56	    return MlflowClient()
57	
58	
59	def detect_kind(ident: str) -> str:
60	    """Classify a row identifier from the tv channel layout.
61	
62	    Returns one of: "run" | "experiment" | "model".
63	
64	      32-hex     -> run        (RUN_ID_RE)
65	      digits-only-> experiment (mlflow assigns non-negative ints)
66	      else       -> model      (registered model name; arbitrary string)
67	
68	    Kept in sync with dot_config/television/executable_mlflow-preview.py:_detect_kind.
69	    """
70	    if RUN_ID_RE.match(ident):
71	        return "run"
72	    if ident.isdigit():
73	        return "experiment"
74	    return "model"
75	
76	
77	def ms_to_iso(ms: int | None) -> str:
78	    """Convert mlflow's millisecond timestamps to local ISO strings.
79	
80	    Returns "-" on missing/invalid input so table renderers can use the
81	    output directly without further None-checks.
82	    """
83	    if not ms:
84	        return "-"
85	    try:
86	        dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(int(ms) / 1000, tz=timezone.utc).astimezone()
87	        return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
88	    except (OverflowError, OSError, ValueError):
89	        return "-"
90	
91

93	    """Current MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI (resolved). Returns "(unset)" if absent."""
94	    import mlflow
95	
96	    return mlflow.get_tracking_uri() or "(unset)"
97	
98	
99	def tracking_uri_is_http() -> bool:
100	    """True when the configured tracking URI uses http(s):// — the only
101	    backend with a web UI that `mlf open` can deep-link into."""
102	    uri = tracking_uri()
103	    return uri.startswith("http://") or uri.startswith("https://")
104	
105	
106	def open_id(ident: str) -> int:
107	    """Open the MLflow web UI deep-link for `ident`. Returns exit code.
108	
109	    Pure helper — no argv parsing. Used by:
110	      - `mlf open <id>` (via _dispatch_open shim in executable_mlf)
111	      - `mlf` TUI's `b` keybinding (in-process call, no subprocess)
112	    """
113	    uri = tracking_uri()
114	    if not tracking_uri_is_http():
115	        print(
116	            f"mlf open: tracking URI is not http(s):// — current: {uri}\n"
117	            "  Set MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http(s)://host:port to use the MLflow web UI.",
118	            file=sys.stderr,
119	        )
120	        return 1
121	
122	    base = uri.rstrip("/")
123	    kind = detect_kind(ident)
124	    if kind == "run":
125	        client = make_client()
126	        try:
127	            run = client.get_run(ident)
128	            exp_id = run.info.experiment_id
129	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
130	            print(
131	                f"mlf open: cannot resolve run '{ident}' — "
132	                f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e).splitlines()[0][:200]}",
133	                file=sys.stderr,
134	            )
135	            return 1
136	        url = f"{base}/#/experiments/{exp_id}/runs/{ident}"
137	    elif kind == "experiment":
138	        url = f"{base}/#/experiments/{ident}"
139	    else:
140	        url = f"{base}/#/models/{ident}"
141	
142	    import webbrowser
143	
144	    print(f"[mlf] open: {url}", file=sys.stderr)
145	    opened = webbrowser.open(url)
146	    if not opened:
147	        print(
148	            "mlf open: no usable browser opener found (open/xdg-open/wslview missing).\n"
149	            f"  URL: {url}",
150	            file=sys.stderr,
151	        )
152	        return 1
153	    return 0
154	
155	
156	def copy_id(payload: str) -> int:
157	    """Copy `payload` to the clipboard. Returns exit code.
158	
159	    Provider chain: pbcopy → wl-copy → xclip → OSC 52 fallback to /dev/tty.
160	    Mirrors the shell snippet in mlflow.toml [actions.copy-id]. Pure helper
161	    so the TUI's `y` action can reuse it without spawning a subprocess.
162	    """
163	    providers = [
164	        ["pbcopy"],
165	        ["wl-copy"],
166	        ["xclip", "-selection", "clipboard"],
167	    ]
168	    for cmd in providers:
169	        if shutil.which(cmd[0]):
170	            try:
171	                subprocess.run(cmd, input=payload, text=True, check=True)
172	            except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
173	                print(
174	                    f"mlf copy: {cmd[0]} failed ({e.returncode}); falling through",
175	                    file=sys.stderr,
176	                )
177	                continue
178	            print(
179	                f"[mlf] copied via {cmd[0]}: {payload[:12]}{'…' if len(payload) > 12 else ''}",
180	                file=sys.stderr,
181	            )
182	            return 0
183	
184	    try:
185	        import base64
186	
187	        b64 = base64.b64encode(payload.encode()).decode()
188	        with open("/dev/tty", "w") as tty:
189	            tty.write(f"\033]52;c;{b64}\007")
190	        print(
191	            f"[mlf] copied via OSC52: {payload[:12]}{'…' if len(payload) > 12 else ''}",
192	            file=sys.stderr,
193	        )
194	        return 0
195	    except OSError as e:
196	        print(
197	            f"mlf copy: no clipboard provider available and OSC52 fallback failed ({e}).\n"
198	            "  Install pbcopy/wl-copy/xclip, or run inside a TTY that supports OSC 52.",
199	            file=sys.stderr,
200	        )
201	        return 1
202	
203	
204	def fetch_histories(
205	    client: "MlflowClient",
206	    run_id: str,
207	    keys: list[str],
208	) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[list[int], list[float]]], list[tuple[str, str]]]:
209	    """Fetch metric history for every key. Skip-on-error per key.
210	
211	    Returns (series, skipped) where:
212	      series  = {key: (steps_sorted, values_aligned), ...}
213	      skipped = [(key, "ExceptionType: message"), ...]
214	
215	    One slow / broken key (commonly a `system.*` metric over a flaky link)
216	    shouldn't abort the whole batch — both the CLI `mlf plot` and the TUI
217	    Plot tab surface skipped keys in a separate warning instead. Bump
218	    MLFLOW_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT for the whole invocation if a host needs
219	    longer per-key reads.
220	    """
221	    series: dict[str, tuple[list[int], list[float]]] = {}
222	    skipped: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
223	    for key in keys:
224	        try:
225	            history = client.get_metric_history(run_id, key)
226	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
227	            skipped.append((key, f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e).splitlines()[0][:80]}"))
228	            continue
229	        if not history:
230	            continue
231	        sorted_hist = sorted(history, key=lambda m: m.step)
232	        steps = [m.step for m in sorted_hist]
233	        values = [m.value for m in sorted_hist]
234	        series[key] = (steps, values)
235	    return series, skipped
236
